definition_zh: 地震；地面震动；（比喻）剧烈动荡
definition_en: a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement along a fault or by volcanic activity
core_image: 铺地的砖石被摇得互相错位，墙上一道裂缝从上到下张开
scene: 小城广场上，铺地的砖石被摇得互相错动，路灯在晃。 The earthquake knocked down two walls but left the square intact.
sceneCN: 这里 earthquake 是「地震」（第 1 个义项：由断层错动或火山活动引起的地面突然震动）；句意为这场地震震塌了两堵墙，却让广场本身完好无损。

pos.zh: 地震；地面震动；（比喻）剧烈动荡

forms.label: 复合形容词（易受地震影响的）

derivatives.zh: 地震（口语截短）；震动、发抖
防震的
抗震的
地震多发的
震撼世界的（由 earth + shake 另构，并非 earthquake 的直接派生）

senses.title: Shaking of the ground
senses.definition: a sudden shaking of the ground caused by the release of strain along a fault
senses.definitionCN: 断层上的应变释放所引起的地面突然震动
senses.example: The earthquake knocked down two walls but left the square intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这场地震震塌了两堵墙，却让广场本身完好无损。
senses.why: earthquake is a plain English compound: earth plus quake, a shaking, so the word names the ground doing what the verb means.
senses.whyCN: earthquake 是朴素的英语复合词：earth「大地」加 quake「震动」，词面就是大地在震。

senses.title: A recorded seismic event
senses.titleCN: 被记录的一次地震事件
senses.definition: a single event entered in a catalogue with a time, location, depth and magnitude
senses.definitionCN: 以时间、位置、深度与震级登记入目录的一次事件
senses.example: The catalogue lists three earthquakes within ten kilometres of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 目录列出该镇十公里范围内的三次地震。
senses.why: once networks record events, earthquake becomes a countable unit of data rather than only an experience.
senses.whyCN: 当台网记录事件之后，earthquake 就不只是人的体验，而成为可计数的数据单位。

senses.title: The main shock of a sequence
senses.definition: the largest event of a sequence, distinguished from the smaller foreshocks and aftershocks
senses.definitionCN: 一次序列中最大的事件，区别于较小的前震与余震
senses.example: The earthquake was followed by forty smaller shocks that night.
senses.exampleCN: 那晚主震之后又发生了四十次较小的震动。
senses.why: a sequence needs a head, so the plain noun came to mean the main shock and the others received prefixed names.
senses.whyCN: 一个序列需要有一个头，因此朴素名词被用来指主震，其余事件则获得带前缀的名称。

senses.title: An induced earthquake
senses.definition: a quake triggered by human activity such as reservoir filling, mining or fluid injection
senses.definitionCN: 由水库蓄水、采矿或流体注入等人类活动触发的地震
senses.example: The injection well caused an earthquake large enough to crack nearby foundations.
senses.exampleCN: 注入井引发了足以震裂附近地基的地震。
senses.why: the mechanism differs but the shaking is the same, so the same noun is kept with an adjective of cause.
senses.whyCN: 机制不同，但震动本身相同，因此保留同一个名词，另加表示成因的形容词。

senses.title: A quake on another world
senses.definition: a seismic event on the Moon, Mars or another solid body
senses.definitionCN: 月球、火星或其他固态天体上的地震事件
senses.example: Instruments left on the Moon recorded an earthquake deep in its crust.
senses.exampleCN: 留在月面的仪器记录到月壳深处的一次地震。
senses.why: the word is extended literally to other bodies, though specialists often prefer moonquake or marsquake.
senses.whyCN: 该词被字面扩展到其他天体，尽管专家往往更爱用 moonquake 或 marsquake。

senses.title: A violent upheaval in society
senses.definition: a sudden, far-reaching change that shakes the established order
senses.definitionCN: 突然而深远、动摇既有秩序的变化
senses.example: The reform was an earthquake in the country's legal tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 这次改革是该国法律传统中的一场地震。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows the physical event wholesale: what shakes is no longer ground but an institution.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻整体借用了物理事件：被摇动的不再是地面，而是一套制度。

senses.title: A shock to a market or organization
senses.titleCN: 对市场或组织的巨大冲击
senses.definition: a disruptive shock that forces rapid restructuring in business or finance
senses.definitionCN: 迫使商业或金融迅速重组的颠覆性冲击
senses.example: The collapse of the carrier was an earthquake for regional airports.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司的倒闭对地区机场是一场地震。
senses.why: economic writing uses the same metaphor because markets, like ground, can lose their bearings.
senses.whyCN: 经济写作使用同一比喻，因为市场与地面一样会失去依托。

senses.title: A disaster category
senses.titleCN: 灾害与保险中的地震类别
senses.definition: a class of natural disaster used in relief planning, insurance and building codes
senses.definitionCN: 用于救援规划、保险与建筑规范的一类自然灾害
senses.example: The policy covers earthquake but not flooding.
senses.exampleCN: 该保单承保地震，但不承保洪水。
senses.why: institutions need to sort hazards into named categories, and the everyday word becomes an administrative one.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要把危险归入有名字的类别，于是日常词变成了行政术语。

intro.en: Earthquake is a native English compound of earth, from Old English eorþe, and quake, from Old English cwacian, to tremble. It is recorded in English from the late thirteenth century and has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: earthquake 是英语本族复合词：earth 来自古英语 eorþe，quake 来自古英语 cwacian「颤抖」。英语文献中自 13 世纪后期即有记录，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Eorþe meant the ground, soil or the world; it survives as earth in modern English and supplies the first element of the compound.
items.cn: eorþe 指大地、土壤或世界；它在现代英语中存为 earth，并构成这个复合词的前一部分。

items.en: Cwacian meant to tremble or shake; its noun quake first meant a trembling of the body before it was applied to the ground.
items.cn: cwacian 意为颤抖或摇动；其名词 quake 最初指身体的发抖，后来才用于地面。

items.en: English joined the two words in the late thirteenth century, at first in forms such as eorþe-cwace, to name the ground shaking.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪后期把两个词拼合，早期形式如 eorþe-cwace，用来指地面震动。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word entered scientific writing, and later catalogues made each event a countable unit.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，该词进入科学写作；后来的地震目录把每次事件变成可计数的单位。

items.en: Modern usage extends earthquake figuratively to political, social and economic shocks that rearrange the ground under an institution.
items.cn: 现代用法把 earthquake 比喻扩展到政治、社会与经济冲击，它们重新排布制度脚下的地面。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the earliest recorded spelling varies between eorþe-cwace and earthquake, and the exact first citation date is given only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：最早的拼写形式在 eorþe-cwace 与 earthquake 之间不同，确切的最早书证年代只能给约数。

note.en: Group one holds the English words built from the same two elements; group two holds terms for shaking events and for upheavals.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样两个成分构成的英语词；第二组是表示震动事件与剧变的词。

entries.definition: The second element used alone: a verb meaning to tremble, and an informal noun for an earthquake.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用的后一成分：动词指颤抖，口语名词指地震。

entries.definition: Built on earth plus shake rather than quake, and now mostly figurative for overwhelmingly important.
entries.definitionCN: 由 earth 加 shake 而非 quake 构成，如今多作比喻指「极其重大」。

entries.definition: Earthquake plus proof in the sense of resistant: built so as not to fail in a quake.
entries.definitionCN: earthquake 加 proof（意为「抗」）：建造得能在震中不失效。

entries.definition: Earthquake plus prone: describing a region likely to experience quakes.
entries.definitionCN: earthquake 加 prone：描述容易发生地震的地区。

entries.definition: A minor earthquake or a continuous shaking; it is usually weaker than an earthquake and can also mean a bodily shake.
entries.definitionCN: 小地震或持续的轻微震动；通常比 earthquake 弱，也可指身体颤抖。

entries.definition: A sudden violent jolt, whether seismic, electrical or emotional; it names the impact rather than the geological event.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的猛烈冲击，可以是地震的、电的或情绪的；指冲击而非地质事件。

entries.definition: A chiefly American Spanish-derived term for an earthquake, common in news from seismic regions.
entries.definitionCN: 主要在美国使用、源自西班牙语的「地震」说法，常见于地震区新闻。

entries.definition: A violent or major change in society or a person's life; unlike earthquake it has no literal geological use.
entries.definitionCN: 社会或个人生活中的剧烈重大变化；与 earthquake 不同，它没有字面地质用法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: earth + quake: the ground doing the trembling.
normal.cn: earth + quake：大地在发抖。

normal.en: The family runs earthquake, earthquakes, quake, earthquake-proof, earthquake-resistant, earthquake-prone.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 earthquake、earthquakes、quake、earthquake-proof、earthquake-resistant、earthquake-prone。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: earthquake damage, earthquake zone, earthquake drill, earthquake insurance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地震破坏、地震区、地震演练、地震保险。

normal.en: News usage: a strong earthquake struck at dawn; the magnitude was revised upward.
normal.cn: 新闻用法：一场强震在黎明袭击；震级被上调。

normal.en: The -quake element also appears in moonquake and marsquake for other bodies.
normal.cn: -quake 成分也出现在指其他天体的 moonquake 与 marsquake 中。

abstract.en: Picture a boardroom table splitting down the middle during a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象一张董事会议桌在投票时从中间裂开。

abstract.en: Picture a price list whose numbers all change while the shopkeeper is still writing.
abstract.cn: 想象店主还在写价目表，上面的数字就全变了。

abstract.en: Picture a constitution whose paragraphs slide past one another like fault blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象一部宪法的条款像断块一样互相错动。

examples.en: The earthquake destroyed the old bridge and cut the only road.
examples.cn: 地震摧毁了那座旧桥，切断了唯一的道路。

examples.en: Engineers design hospitals to remain open after a major earthquake.
examples.cn: 工程师把医院设计成在大地震后仍能运转。

examples.en: The discovery of the letters was an earthquake in the study of the period.
examples.cn: 这批信件的发现使该时期的研究发生了地震般的震荡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「earth（大地）+ quake（抖）」——大地发抖 → 地震

root: 英语本族复合词：古英语 eorþe「大地」+ cwacian「颤抖」的名词 quake；无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shaking from ground to catalogue: the physical event, the recorded event, the main shock, the human-caused and off-world variants, then society, markets and finally the administrative category.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一场震动从地面走进目录：物理事件、被记录的事件、主震、人为与地外变体，再到社会、市场，最后成为行政类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paving stones shifted out of line and a crack opening down a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺地砖石错位，墙体从上到下裂开。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL EVENT: the ground moves because strain is released.
branches.cn: 物理事件：应变释放，地面因此移动。

branches.en: THE CATALOGUE: an event becomes a row of data, with a head and smaller followers.
branches.cn: 目录：事件变成一行数据，有头部，也有较小的跟随者。

branches.en: CHANGED CAUSE AND PLACE: humans can trigger it, and other worlds can host it.
branches.cn: 成因与场所的变换：人类可以触发它，别的世界也可以承载它。

branches.en: METAPHOR: institutions and markets are shaken until their old alignments fail.
branches.cn: 比喻：制度与市场被摇到旧有对齐失效。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATIVE BOX: the event becomes a category that policies and codes refer to.
branches.cn: 行政归类：事件变成一个保单与规范可以引用的类别。

intro.en: Earthquake is a native compound of two free morphemes, and its second element also lives alone as a verb and an informal noun.
intro.cn: earthquake 是由两个自由语素构成的本族复合词，其第二成分也能独立作动词与口语名词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin elements are involved: both halves are inherited Germanic words, though Latin terra and quatere are only semantic parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 不涉及拉丁成分：两半都是继承的日耳曼语词；拉丁 terra 与 quatere 只是语义上的平行词，并非来源。

items.example: Earth supplies the object being shaken.
items.exampleCN: earth 提供被摇动的对象。

items.meaning: a shaking of a named body
items.example: Moonquake and marsquake use the same element.
items.exampleCN: moonquake 与 marsquake 使用同一成分。

items.example: The earthquake lasted less than a minute.
items.exampleCN: 那次地震持续不到一分钟。

items.example: The region records hundreds of earthquakes each year.
items.exampleCN: 该地区每年记录数百次地震。

items.example: The shelter is earthquake-proof by design.

items.example: The ruling was earthshaking for the industry.

definition_zh: 毛巾；手巾；浴巾；纸巾
definition_en: a piece of thick cloth used for drying your body, hands, or dishes
core_image: 一条搭在木架上、还在滴水的厚布
scene: 洗完手之后水还在往下淌，架子上的厚布被拿起来按在掌心。 He reached for the towel and wiped his hands twice.
sceneCN: 这里 towel 是「毛巾、手巾」（第 1 个义项：用于擦干身体或手的一块厚布）；句意为他拿起毛巾把手擦了两遍。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「毛巾布；毛巾料」
由过去分词转化，义为「用毛巾擦干的」

senses.title: Cloth for drying the hands or face
senses.definition: a small thick cloth kept by a basin for wiping wet hands or face
senses.definitionCN: 放在盆边用来擦干湿手或脸的小块厚布
senses.example: There is a clean towel hanging beside the sink.
senses.exampleCN: 水槽旁边挂着一条干净的毛巾。
senses.why: The word names the cloth that does the drying, and this household use is the oldest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指执行擦干动作的那块布，这种家常用途是最古老的日常义项。

senses.title: The large cloth used after a bath
senses.definition: a big towel that wraps the whole body after washing
senses.definitionCN: 洗完澡后能裹住整个身体的大毛巾
senses.example: She came out of the shower wrapped in a towel.
senses.exampleCN: 她裹着浴巾从淋浴间走出来。
senses.why: The same cloth grows to body size, and English simply keeps the one word for both sizes.
senses.whyCN: 同一种布长大到身体尺寸，英语仍用一个词兼指两种规格。

senses.title: A disposable paper square
senses.definition: a sheet of absorbent paper used once for drying or wiping
senses.definitionCN: 一次性使用、用来擦干的吸水纸
senses.example: He grabbed a paper towel to mop up the spilled coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 他抽了一张纸巾去擦洒出来的咖啡。
senses.why: When paper took over the drying job, the old cloth name simply moved onto it with paper in front.
senses.whyCN: 当纸接过擦干的任务，旧的布名只要前面加个 paper 就直接移用过去了。

senses.title: To rub dry with a towel
senses.definition: to rub a person, animal, or object dry with a towel
senses.definitionCN: 用毛巾把人、动物或物体擦干
senses.example: She toweled her hair quickly and ran for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 她匆匆把头发擦干就往公交站跑。
senses.why: Any tool can be turned into a verb, so the cloth becomes the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 任何工具都能转为动词，于是这块布就成了「用它」这个动作。

senses.title: Surrender in the idiom
senses.definition: in the phrase throw in the towel, to admit defeat and stop trying
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 throw in the towel 中表示承认失败、停止努力
senses.example: After three failed attempts he threw in the towel.
senses.exampleCN: 三次尝试失败后，他认输了。
senses.why: A boxer's corner threw a towel into the ring to end the fight, so the cloth came to mean giving up.
senses.whyCN: 拳击台的教练往擂台上扔毛巾表示终止比赛，于是这条布就成了「放弃」的意思。

intro.en: Towel comes from Old French toaille, a cloth for washing, which goes back to a Germanic word for a washing cloth, probably influenced in form by Latin words for cloth.
intro.cn: towel 来自古法语 toaille（洗涤用的布），其更早来源是日耳曼语表示「擦洗布」的词，词形大概受拉丁语中表示布的词影响。

items.en: A Germanic word for a washing cloth, related to the verb to wash, is generally taken as the ultimate source.
items.cn: 一般认为其最终来源是日耳曼语中表示「洗涤布」的词，与表示「洗」的动词相关。

items.en: Frankish speech carries the word into Old French, where it appears as toaille with the meaning bath cloth.
items.cn: 法兰克人的语言把这个词带进古法语，写成 toaille，意为「浴布」。

items.en: Medieval Latin documents use toallia and tuallia for table and hand cloths, likely borrowed back from the French form.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁文献用 toallia、tuallia 指桌布和擦手布，大概又是从法语形式借回去的。

items.en: English adopts the word as towaille and later settles on towel for the cloth kept by the basin.
items.cn: 英语先写成 towaille，后来固定为 towel，指放在盆边的擦布。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word attaches to paper sheets, and the boxing phrase throw in the towel appears.
items.cn: 十九世纪这个词用到纸制品上，拳击习语 throw in the towel 也在这时出现。

items.en: The verb to towel develops in the same period from the noun, first for people then for dogs and hair.
items.cn: 动词 towel 也在同一时期由名词发展出来，先指擦人，后指擦狗和头发。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the ending or the towel-like shape, and the near-meaning group gathers cloths used in the bathroom or kitchen.
note.cn: 形近组收集词尾相同或形状像毛巾的词，近义组则收入浴室与厨房用的布。

entries.definitionCN: 塔；高楼，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a part of the intestine
entries.definitionCN: 肠，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a speech sound such as a or o
entries.definitionCN: 元音，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the cloth towels are made of
entries.definitionCN: 毛巾布

entries.definition: soft cloth used for washing the face
entries.definitionCN: 擦脸用的软布；绒布

entries.definition: a cloth or paper used at meals
entries.definitionCN: 餐巾；纸巾

entries.definition: soft paper used for wiping the nose
entries.definitionCN: 面巾纸

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the way the word has moved from cloth to paper and from noun to verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从本词「由布到纸、由名词到动词」的迁移方式入手。

normal.en: Bath towel, hand towel, paper towel: the material or the use goes in front of the same cloth.
normal.cn: bath towel、hand towel、paper towel，材料或用途一律放在这块布前面。

normal.en: The -el ending is the same as in the borrowed French cloth words, not a suffix of meaning.
normal.cn: 词尾 -el 和借入的法语布名一样，只是形式，不表示意义。

normal.en: Towel can be a verb because every tool can become the act of using it.
normal.cn: towel 可以作动词，因为每件工具都能变成使用它的动作。

normal.en: Throw in the towel comes from boxing corners, where a thrown cloth ended the fight.
normal.cn: throw in the towel 来自拳击教练席，被扔出的布会终止比赛。

normal.en: Paper towel shows the word's willingness to change material: cloth first, paper later.
normal.cn: paper towel 显示这个词乐于更换材质：先是布，后来是纸。

abstract.en: Picture a wet hand and the white square that turns it dry in two seconds.
abstract.cn: 想象一只湿手和那块两秒就把它擦白的方布。

abstract.en: Think of a towel on a rail, still heavy with the last person's water.
abstract.cn: 想一条搭在架上的毛巾，还带着上一位使用者的水。

abstract.en: A towel is a small borrowed dryness that you hand back after use.
abstract.cn: 毛巾是可以借用、用完还回去的一小块「干」。

examples.en: Pass me a towel, please.
examples.cn: 请递给我一条毛巾。

examples.en: He toweled the dog dry at the door.
examples.cn: 他在门口把狗擦干了。

examples.en: After two hours of arguing, she threw in the towel.
examples.cn: 争了两个小时后，她认输了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「套哦」——把手套进去擦干，哦，水全没了。

root: 日耳曼语「擦洗布」（与「洗」的动词相关）→ 法兰克语 → 古法语 toaille → 中古英语 towaille → 英语 towel。同族词有 towelling、toweled。

sensesIntro.en: The entry follows one cloth through its sizes and materials, then through its change from noun to verb, and ends at the boxing ring where the same cloth means defeat.
sensesIntro.cn: 本词跟随同一块布，走过不同尺寸与材质，再由名词转为动词，最后来到拳击台上，用同一块布表示认输。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick absorbent cloth held against wet skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块厚而吸水的布贴在湿皮肤上。

branches.en: The small cloth beside the basin.
branches.cn: 盆边的小块擦布。

branches.en: The body-sized cloth after a bath.
branches.cn: 洗澡后裹身的大布。

branches.en: The paper version of the drying cloth.
branches.cn: 擦干布的纸质版本。

branches.en: The cloth turned into an action.
branches.cn: 布转为动作。

branches.en: The thrown cloth that ends a fight.
branches.cn: 被扔出去终止比赛的布。

intro.en: The word is a borrowing without a productive English suffix, but its members show the -el of borrowed French nouns and the -ing of the continuing form.
intro.cn: 本词是借词，没有能产的英语后缀，但词族里能看出法语借入名词的 -el 与持续体的 -ing。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin records the word as toallia, borrowed back from French, so the Latin entries are the documentary forms rather than true roots.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁文献把这个词记作 toallia，是从法语借回去的，因此下面的拉丁词条是文献形式而非真正词根。

items.example: Toaille is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: toaille 是英语本词的直接来源。

items.example: The ending appears in borrowed cloth names.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾出现在借入的布名中。

items.example: Towelling is the cloth the towel is made of.
Toweled is the past of the verb.
Bath towel is the large size.
Hand towel is the small size.
Paper towel replaces cloth with sheet.
items.exampleCN: paper towel 用纸片替代布。

items.meaning: a bar to hang things on
items.example: A towel rail holds the cloths.

latinEntries.meaning: a variant form of the same cloth word
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同一布名词的变体形式

definition_zh: 选择；挑选；决定；情愿
definition_en: to pick out from two or more possibilities; to decide to do something
core_image: 伸出手，从一堆东西里取出那一个
scene: 图书馆里，我在两本喜欢的书之间犹豫了很久。 You can choose any two books to borrow.
sceneCN: 这里 choose 是「挑选」（第 1 个义项：从多个可能中选出）；句意是你可以任选两本书借走。

derivatives.zh: choose 的名词形式，义为「选择；选项」
由 choose 加后缀 -y 构成，义为「挑剔的」
由 choose 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「挑选者」

senses.title: To pick out one from many
senses.definition: to take the one you want from two or more things
senses.definitionCN: 从两个以上事物中取出想要的那个
senses.example: Please choose a partner for the game.
senses.exampleCN: 请为游戏选一位搭档。
senses.why: The basic sense is the hand and mind picking one thing out.
senses.whyCN: 基本义项就是伸手和用心挑出一个东西。

senses.title: To decide to do something
senses.definition: to decide that you will do something
senses.definitionCN: 下定决心要做某事
senses.example: He chose to walk home in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 他决定冒雨步行回家。
senses.why: Picking an action is picking with the whole life, so decide grows from pick.
senses.whyCN: 挑选一个行动就是「挑选」放大到人生层面，决定义由此生长。

senses.title: To prefer; to think fit
senses.definition: to prefer or consider it right to do something
senses.definitionCN: 宁愿做或认为这样做合适
senses.example: You may stay if you choose.
senses.exampleCN: 你愿意的话可以留下。
senses.why: Free will turns a simple pick into a statement of preference.
senses.whyCN: 自由意志让单纯的挑选变成意愿的表达。

intro.en: Choose comes straight from Old English and has cousins across the Germanic languages.
intro.cn: choose 直接来自古英语，在各日耳曼语中都有亲戚。

items.en: Old English cēosan meant to choose or to test by tasting or picking.
items.cn: 古英语 cēosan 义为「挑选」，或通过品尝、拣选来甄别。

items.en: Old Norse kjósa, a close cousin, kept the same meaning in Scandinavia.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 kjósa 是近亲，在斯堪的纳维亚保留同义。

items.en: It traces back to Germanic *keusan-, whose deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 它可追溯到日耳曼语 *keusan-，更早来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English used chesen and chesen with past form chose.
items.cn: 中古英语作 chesen，过去式作 chose。

items.en: Modern English keeps the irregular pair chose and chosen.
items.cn: 现代英语保留不规则变化 chose 和 chosen。

note.en: The first group gathers words close in shape or sound; the second gathers picking words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收挑选类词。

entries.definition: The past tense of choose.
entries.definitionCN: choose 的过去式，拼写仅差一字母。

entries.definition: The past participle of choose.
entries.definitionCN: choose 的过去分词，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A food made from milk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「奶酪」，词形与 choose 相近。

entries.definition: To choose carefully from a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「精选」，较正式。

entries.definition: To choose casually.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挑选」，较随意。

entries.definition: To choose by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选举」，通过投票挑选。

normalIntro.en: Remember choose through its family of forms.
normalIntro.cn: 通过形式变化记忆 choose。

normal.en: choose has oo now, but chose and chosen have o-e.
normal.cn: choose 用 oo，chose 和 chosen 用 o-e。

normal.en: say CHOO-ze with a long zoo sound.
normal.cn: 长音读如 zoo，CHOO-ze。

normal.en: choice is the noun; choosy means picky.
normal.cn: choice 是名词，choosy 义为挑剔。

normal.en: pick and choose means to be fussy.
normal.cn: pick and choose 指挑三拣四。

normal.en: you cannot choose but wait means you must wait.
normal.cn: cannot choose but wait 即只能等待。

abstract.en: See your hand hovering over a box of colours.
abstract.cn: 想象手在一盒彩笔上方悬停。

abstract.en: Feel the weight of taking one and leaving the rest.
abstract.cn: 感受取一舍余时那一点重量。

abstract.en: Hear the yes click shut after long thinking.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见思虑许久后「就这么定了」的轻响。

examples.en: You may choose two stickers from the sheet.
examples.cn: 你可以从这张贴纸上选两张。

examples.en: She chose the window seat on the train.
examples.cn: 她选了火车上的靠窗座位。

examples.en: We are choosing a name for the class rabbit.
examples.cn: 我们正在给班级兔子选名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丘斯」——丘丘挑零食时哼着「就这个」斯斯地说完，choose 就定了。

root: 古英语 cēosan（挑选）→ 日耳曼语 *keusan-（来源不确定）→ 中古英语 chesen → 现代英语 choose；同族词有古诺斯语 kjósa、名词 choice、形容词 choosy。

sensesIntro.en: Choose starts as picking a thing, widens to deciding an action, then to free preference.
sensesIntro.cn: choose 从挑一件东西出发，扩大到决定做某事，再到自由意愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching into a group and taking one
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸入一堆东西取出一个

branches.en: Selecting a concrete thing
branches.cn: 挑出具体的东西

branches.en: Deciding on an action
branches.cn: 决定一个行动

branches.en: Expressing free preference
branches.cn: 表达自由意愿

branches.en: Choosing people for a role
branches.cn: 挑选人员担任角色

branches.en: Choosing between paths
branches.cn: 在道路之间抉择

intro.en: Choose builds a small family of verb, noun and adjective.
intro.cn: choose 生成了动词、名词和形容词的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Choose is Germanic through and through, with no Latin root inside.
latinIntro.cn: choose 是纯日耳曼词，不含拉丁词根。

items.meaning: the act or result of choosing

items.example: Select a topic for the essay.

definition_zh: 诙谐的；幽默的；滑稽的；爱开玩笑的
definition_en: funny or amusing, or describing a person who likes to make people laugh
core_image: 把一件平常的事讲得让人笑出声
scene: 课堂上气氛很沉闷。 The teacher told a humorous story and the whole class laughed.
sceneCN: 这里 humorous 是「诙谐的、引人发笑的」（第 1 个义项：内容有趣好笑）；句意：老师讲了一个幽默的故事，全班都笑了。

derivatives.zh: 幽默；由词根 humor 加后缀而来，指可笑的气质或内容
诙谐地；幽默地；形容词加副词后缀
幽默作家；词根加表人的后缀

senses.title: Funny and amusing
senses.definition: funny and making people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 有趣的、让人发笑的
senses.example: He kept a humorous tone even in serious talks.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在严肃谈话中他也保持幽默的语气。
senses.why: Humor is the substance that makes people laugh, so the adjective simply says the thing is full of that substance.
senses.whyCN: humor 本身指可笑的东西，形容词只是说这件事充满了这种东西，所以能引人发笑。

senses.title: Playful in manner
senses.definition: describing a person who often jokes and sees the funny side
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人爱开玩笑、总看到滑稽的一面
senses.example: My uncle is a humorous man at family dinners.
senses.exampleCN: 家宴上我叔叔是个爱开玩笑的人。
senses.why: The word moves from content to person: someone whose speech is constantly full of humor.
senses.whyCN: 词义从内容移到人：某人说话总是充满幽默感。

senses.title: Comically odd or exaggerated
senses.definition: odd or exaggerated in an amusing way
senses.definitionCN: 以好笑的方式显得古怪或夸张
senses.example: The film gives a humorous picture of office life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影对办公室生活做了滑稽的刻画。
senses.why: When a portrayal exaggerates reality until it becomes funny, the result is labeled humorous.
senses.whyCN: 当描写把现实夸张到令人发笑时，成果就被贴上幽默的标签。

senses.title: Intended as a joke
senses.definition: said or done in a joking way rather than seriously
senses.definitionCN: 以玩笑方式说出或做出，而非当真
senses.example: It was a humorous comment, not a real criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是句玩笑话，不是真的批评。
senses.why: An utterance can carry humor as its purpose rather than its effect, so the adjective marks intent.
senses.whyCN: 话语可以以幽默为目的而不只是效果，形容词由此标记意图。

intro.en: Humorous comes from Latin humor, bodily fluid, through Old French and English humor. The four bodily fluids of medieval medicine were thought to shape mood, and a moody or capricious temperament came to be called humor, from which the modern sense of comedy developed.
intro.cn: humorous 源自拉丁语 humor「体液」，经古法语与英语 humor 传入。中世纪医学认为四种体液决定性情，「反复无常的脾气」被称为 humor，现代「滑稽可笑」的义项由此发展而来。

items.en: Latin humor meant moisture or bodily fluid, one of the fluids ancient doctors believed controlled health and temper.
items.cn: 拉丁语 humor 指湿气或体液，古代医生认为这些液体控制健康与性情。

items.en: Old French humur carried the same bodily meaning into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 humur 带着同样的体液义传入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English humor first meant bodily fluid, then a fixed temper or mood, as in being in a good humor.
items.cn: 中古英语 humor 先指体液，后指固定的心境，如 in a good humor「心情好」。

items.en: By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries humor meant an odd or amusing temperament, then anything that provokes laughter.
items.cn: 十七八世纪起 humor 指古怪有趣的性情，进而指一切引人发笑之物。

items.en: Humorous was formed in the seventeenth century as the adjective of humor and spread through literature and everyday speech.
items.cn: humorous 于十七世纪作为 humor 的形容词被造出，经文学与日常用语传播开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the humor family and a falsely similar word. The meaning group collects other words for things that make people laugh.
note.cn: 形近组收录 humor 词族与一个貌似相关的词；词义组收集其他表示引人发笑之物的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being amusing, or a person's mood.
entries.definitionCN: 幽默；心情。是本词的名词基础。

entries.definition: a writer or performer who specializes in humor.
entries.definitionCN: 幽默作家或演员。由词根加表人后缀构成。

entries.definition: the bone of the upper arm. It only looks and sounds similar; it is a Latin anatomy word, not related to jokes.
entries.definitionCN: 上臂骨。只是拼写与读音相近，属解剖学词汇，与玩笑无关。

entries.definition: amusing in a direct, everyday way; broader and more casual than humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 好笑的。比 humorous 更口语、更宽泛。

entries.definition: entertaining and making you smile, often more gently funny.
entries.definitionCN: 逗乐的。常指温和的、让人微笑的有趣。

entries.definition: clever and quick with words; funny through intelligence.
entries.definitionCN: 机智的。靠言语巧妙取胜的幽默。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build humorous from humor plus the adjective ending, and link the family of humor, humorist and humorousness.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 humorous 拆成 humor 加形容词后缀，并串起 humor、humorist 等词族。

normal.en: Split it: humor + -ous. Full of humor, so funny.
normal.cn: 拆开看：humor 加 -ous。充满幽默，所以好笑。

normal.en: Humorist is a humor artist; humorous is what the artist's work is.
normal.cn: humorist 是幽默艺术家；humorous 形容这位艺术家的作品。

normal.en: Latin humor was a body fluid; old doctors said your fluids set your mood, and a bright mood laughs easily.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 humor 是体液；旧时医生说体液决定心情，心情明快就容易发笑。

normal.en: in a good humor means in a good mood; the family never lost that old sense.
normal.cn: in a good humor 意为心情好；这个词族至今保留着那个旧义。

normal.en: Watch the trap: humerus is an arm bone, not a joke bone.
normal.cn: 小心陷阱：humerus 是臂骨，不是「笑骨」。

abstract.en: One image: a teacher lifts a dull lesson and the class bursts out laughing.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：老师把沉闷的课讲活了，全班笑出声。

abstract.en: Think of humor as a fluid that pours into a story and makes it lighter.
abstract.cn: 把 humor 想成一种液体，倒进故事里让它变轻快。

abstract.en: Feel the scale: witty is sharp, amusing is gentle, humorous is the neutral middle.
abstract.cn: 感受尺度：witty 尖锐、amusing 温和，humorous 居中。

examples.en: She wrote a humorous column about city life.
examples.cn: 她写了一个关于城市生活的幽默专栏。

examples.en: His humorous answer eased the tension in the room.
examples.cn: 他诙谐的回答缓和了屋里的紧张气氛。

examples.en: Good speeches often open with a humorous remark.
examples.cn: 好的演讲常以一句幽默的话开场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「有墨若斯」：肚里很有墨水的人若开口，就幽默了。

root: 拉丁语 humor「体液、湿气」，经古法语 humur 与中古英语 humor「体液→心境→滑稽可笑」，加形容词后缀 -ous 构成 humorous「幽默的」。词义演变路径为「体液→性情→引人发笑」。

sensesIntro.en: Humorous spreads from content to people to intent: a thing can be funny, a person can be fond of jokes, a portrayal can be comically exaggerated, and a remark can be meant as a joke rather than seriously.
sensesIntro.cn: humorous 从内容铺到人再到意图：事物可以有趣，人可以爱开玩笑，刻画可以滑稽夸张，话也可以只是玩笑而非当真。

core.en: A bright mood-fluid poured into a thing, a person or a remark, making it laughable.
core.cn: 把明快的性情之液倒进事物、人或话语，使其引人发笑。

branches.en: FUNNY CONTENT: a thing or remark that provokes laughter, on purpose or by effect.
branches.cn: 有趣的内容：故意或事实上引人发笑的事物或话语。

branches.en: PLAYFUL PERSON: someone who sees the funny side and jokes often.
branches.cn: 爱开玩笑的人：总看到滑稽一面、常开玩笑的人。

branches.en: COMIC PORTRAYAL: an exaggerated, amusing picture of reality.
branches.cn: 滑稽刻画：对现实夸张而有趣的描绘。

branches.en: TEMPER: the old sense of humor as mood survives in a humorous turn of mind.
branches.cn: 性情：humor 的旧义「心境」保存在幽默的气质里。

branches.en: TONE: humor as a stylistic register, light instead of heavy.
branches.cn: 风格：幽默作为一种笔调，轻盈而非沉重。

intro.en: Humorous is humor plus -ous. The family keeps the mood sense alive in phrases like in a good humor.
intro.cn: humorous 由 humor 加 -ous 构成。这个词族在 in a good humor 等短语里保留着心境的旧义。

latinIntro.en: Latin entries show the bodily-fluid noun that slowly turned into the comedy noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目展示那个由体液慢慢变成「滑稽」的名词。

items.example: The narrator keeps a humorous voice.
items.exampleCN: 叙述者保持着幽默的口吻。

items.example: She has a fine sense of humor.

items.meaning: a person who writes or performs humor
items.example: The humorist signed copies of his new book.
items.exampleCN: 那位幽默作家为读者签名。

items.example: He humorously called the office a zoo.
items.exampleCN: 他诙谐地把办公室比作动物园。

items.example: The essay's humorousness hides its serious point.
items.exampleCN: 文章的幽默感掩盖着严肃的论点。

items.example: Our good-humored guide joked all day.
items.exampleCN: 我们和气的导游一路说笑。
他是带着坏心情说话的。

items.meaning: relating to bodily fluids, in old medicine
items.example: Ancient doctors held a humoral theory of disease.
items.exampleCN: 古代医生信奉体液致病说。

definition_zh: 家伙；人；各位；（动词）取笑；嘲讽
definition_en: a man, or any person in a casual way; to make fun of someone
core_image: 一群朋友勾肩搭背走在街上，随口互相打招呼
scene: 操场上几个同学刚打完篮球，正互相开着玩笑往回走。 Hey guys, let us get some water before the next game.
sceneCN: 这里 guy 是「家伙、各位」（第 1 个义项：随口称呼的人）；句意是招呼同伴们在下一场球前喝点水。

derivatives.zh: 由 guy 加 -ing 构成，义为「嘲弄；取笑」（英式口语）
由 guy + rope 构成，义为「（帐篷）拉索」，另义下的合成词

senses.title: A man or person
senses.definition: a man, or anyone, talked about in a casual friendly way
senses.definitionCN: 以随意口吻谈到的男人或任何人
senses.example: That guy in the red jacket is my cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 穿红夹克的那个家伙是我表哥。
senses.why: Friends point with a grin rather than a name, so the casual pointer word is born.
senses.whyCN: 朋友间笑着指认而非称呼名字，随意的指称词由此而生。

senses.title: A group greeting
senses.definition: people addressed together, as in you guys
senses.definitionCN: 一起招呼的众人，如 you guys
senses.example: Thanks, guys, for helping me move.
senses.exampleCN: 各位，谢谢帮我搬家。
senses.why: One casual word stretched to hold a whole crowd at once.
senses.whyCN: 一个随口词延伸开来，一口气罩住一群人。

senses.title: To make fun of
senses.definition: to tease or mock someone, chiefly in British English
senses.definitionCN: 取笑或嘲讽某人，主要用于英式英语
senses.example: The class guied his new haircut gently.
senses.exampleCN: 全班善意地取笑他的新发型。
senses.why: Pointing at a person easily slides into pointing fun at one.
senses.whyCN: 用手指人很容易滑向用手指笑，指认变成揶揄。

senses.title: A rope holding something steady
senses.definition: a rope or wire that keeps a pole or tent steady
senses.definitionCN: 固定桅杆或帐篷的绳索
senses.example: Tighten the guy before the wind rises.
senses.exampleCN: 起风前拉紧牵索。
senses.why: A separate old word guy lived in rigging and later merged into the same spelling.
senses.whyCN: 另一个古老的 guy（拉索）词在绳缆行当里存在，后来并入同一拼写。

senses.title: An effigy burned on a holiday
senses.definition: a model of a person burned on Guy Fawkes Night
senses.definitionCN: 英国盖伊·福克斯之夜焚烧的人偶
senses.example: Children showed their guy for a penny.

senses.title: The heavier side of a comparison: more important
senses.titleCN: 比较中更重的一侧：更重要
senses.definition: more important, more powerful, or more effective than other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中更重要、更有力量或更有效
senses.example: Tourism is a major source of income for the island.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这个岛的主要收入来源。
senses.why: Latin maior is the comparative of magnus 'great'. The word begins as a weighing: two things are compared and one side is heavier. Importance is the first thing this comparison measures, before size or number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maior 是 magnus“大”的比较级。这个词的起点是一次称量：两样东西相比，有一侧更重。这个比较最先量的是重要性，然后才是尺寸或数量。

senses.title: Greater in scale or quantity
senses.definition: larger in size, number, or extent when measured against others
senses.definitionCN: 与其他事物相比，在尺寸、数量或范围上更大
senses.example: A major portion of the budget goes to salaries.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的一大部分用于工资。
senses.why: The same scale now reads quantity rather than rank. Because maior already carries 'more', careful English does not say 'very major': a big city can be a major city, but major itself never means merely big.
senses.whyCN: 同一架天平现在量的是数量而不是位次。由于 maior 本身已含“更多”，规范的英语不说 very major：大城市可以是 major city，但 major 本身从不只表示“尺寸大”。

senses.title: Serious enough to matter: medical and risk use
senses.titleCN: 重大到需要重视：医疗与风险用法
senses.definition: serious in effect or risk, especially of surgery, illness, damage, or change
senses.definitionCN: 在后果或风险上严重，尤用于手术、疾病、损害或变化
senses.example: The patient needs major surgery on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人需要接受膝关节大手术。
senses.why: In medicine the comparison is between procedures that threaten the body and those that do not. A major operation is not simply bigger; it carries a higher risk, so the comparative becomes a judgement of severity.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，比较的两端是威胁身体的手术与不威胁身体的手术。大手术不只是“更大”，而是风险更高，因此比较级变成了一种严重程度的判断。

senses.title: Music: the scale a half-step greater
senses.definition: of a scale, key, or chord built on a major third, sounding brighter and more stable than the minor
senses.definitionCN: 指以大三级为基础的音阶、调或和弦，听感比小调明亮、稳定
senses.example: The piece moves from a minor key into a bright major key.
senses.exampleCN: 这首曲子从小调转入明亮的大调。
senses.why: Music borrowed the word in the 1690s because a major interval is a half-step 'greater' than the minor one. The comparison is now measured on the keyboard rather than on a scale of importance.
senses.whyCN: 音乐在 17 世纪 90 年代借用这个词，因为大三度比小三度“多”一个半音。此时比较是在键盘上量的，而不是在重要性的尺度上量的。

senses.title: University: the subject weighted most
senses.definition: the main subject a student specializes in, or to specialize in that subject
senses.definitionCN: 学生专攻的主修科目，或专攻该科目
senses.example: She majored in economics and minored in statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 她主修经济学，辅修统计学。
senses.why: A degree is a set of subjects, and one of them is weighted more heavily than the rest. The noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890 and the verb by 1910, both keeping the heavier side of the balance.
senses.whyCN: 一个学位由若干科目组成，其中一门的分量重于其余。名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，动词义记录于 1910 年，两者都保留了天平上更重的那一侧。

senses.title: Military rank: the senior officer
senses.definition: an officer rank above captain and below lieutenant colonel
senses.definitionCN: 高于上尉、低于中校的军官军衔
senses.example: The major briefed the company commanders before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 少校在黎明前向各连长做了简报。
senses.why: The rank came through French major, short for sergent-major, from Medieval Latin major 'chief officer'. In a body of officers one is marked as the senior one, so the comparative is used as a title.
senses.whyCN: 这个军衔经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）来自中世纪拉丁语 major“首席军官”。在一群军官中有一人被标为资历更高者，于是比较级被用作头衔。

senses.title: Legal adulthood: the older side of the line
senses.titleCN: 法定成年：年龄界线另一侧的人
senses.definition: a person who has reached the age of legal adulthood, or the state of being of full legal age
senses.definitionCN: 已达到法定成年年龄的人，或处于完全法定成年状态
senses.example: A minor cannot sign the contract; a major can.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人不能签这份合同，成年人可以。
senses.why: Medieval Latin major also named 'an elder, an adult'. Law needs a line between those who can bind themselves and those who cannot, and major marks the person on the older side of that line.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 major 也指“年长者、成年人”。法律需要在能为自己负责与不能负责的人之间划一条线，major 标记的就是这条线年长一侧的人。

senses.title: The top tier: major leagues and the majors
senses.titleCN: 最高层级：大联盟与顶级行列
senses.definition: in sport and business, the highest level of competition or the largest organizations, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在体育与商业中，最高级别的赛事或最大的机构，常用复数
senses.example: He spent six seasons in the majors before returning to coach.
senses.exampleCN: 他在顶级联赛打了六个赛季，之后回去当教练。
senses.why: Major league is recorded in baseball by 1892. The comparison now runs between leagues rather than people: one circuit is the greater one, and 'the majors' became shorthand for the top tier in any field.
senses.whyCN: major league 在棒球中记录于 1892 年。此时比较发生在联盟之间而不是人之间：有一个联盟是“更大”的，于是 the majors 成了任何领域顶级行列的简称。

senses.title: Usage boundary: major is not simply big
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：major 不等于“尺寸大”
senses.definition: major describes importance or seriousness rather than physical size alone; it is not graded with very, and minor is its usual opposite
senses.definitionCN: major 描述重要性或严重性，而不只是物理尺寸；它不用 very 分级，其通常的反义词是 minor
senses.example: The storm caused major delays, though the airport itself is not very big.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成了严重延误，尽管机场本身并不大。
senses.why: Because maior is already a comparative, 'very major' is redundant in careful use. A major city is important, not necessarily large; a big city is large, not necessarily important. Major and minor split one scale into two sides.
senses.whyCN: 由于 maior 已是比较级，规范的用法中 very major 是冗余的。major city 是重要的城市，不一定面积大；big city 是面积大的城市，不一定重要。major 与 minor 把同一把尺子分成两侧。

intro.en: Major is the comparative form of the Latin word for 'great'. It entered English around 1300 as a word of rank, and later spread to quantity, music, universities, armies and leagues — always marking the heavier side of a comparison.
intro.cn: major 是拉丁语“大”的比较级形式。它约在 1300 年进入英语，最初表示位次高低，后来扩展到数量、音乐、大学、军队和联赛——始终标记比较中更重的一侧。

items.en: First recorded in English as majour, 'greater, more important or effective, leading, principal'. From c. 1300 it also named an elder or an adult.
items.cn: 最早以 majour 记录于英语，意为“更大的、更重要的或更有效的、领先的、主要的”。约 1300 年起也指年长者或成年人。

items.en: From Latin maior (earlier *magios), the irregular comparative of magnus 'large, great'. A comparative built on a suppletive stem, not on a regular -ior suffix added to magnus.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maior（更早作 *magios），是 magnus“大”的不规则比较级。它是建立在异干互补词干上的比较级，并不是在 magnus 后加规则的 -ior。

items.en: magnus and maior are traced to PIE *meg- 'great', the same root behind magnify, magnitude and master. This reconstruction is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: magnus 与 maior 被追溯到原始印欧语 *meg-“大”，也是 magnify、magnitude、master 的词根。这一重构属于一般认为，而非确证。

items.en: The sense 'greater in quantity, number, or extent' is recorded from the 1590s, extending the comparison from rank to measurable scale.
items.cn: “数量、数目或范围更大”的义项记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，把比较从位次扩展到可测量的规模。

items.en: The military rank appears in the 1640s via French major, short for sergent-major. The musical sense follows in the 1690s, from the idea of an interval a half-step 'greater' than the minor.
items.cn: 军衔义在 17 世纪 40 年代经法语 major（sergent-major 的缩略）出现。音乐义随后在 17 世纪 90 年代出现，来自“比小调音程多半音”的观念。

items.en: The academic noun 'subject of specialization' is recorded by 1890, major league by 1892, and the verb 'to focus one's studies' by 1910 in American English.
items.cn: 学术名词义“专业”记录于 1890 年，major league 记录于 1892 年，动词义“专注学业”记录于 1910 年，属美式英语。

note.en: The first group shares the maior / magnus line or looks close to it. The second group separates words for rank, importance, size and degree, which English often uses interchangeably and often should not.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maior／magnus 这条线，或词形接近。第二组区分位次、重要性、尺寸与程度——英语常把它们混用，而很多时候不该混用。

entries.definition: the larger number or part; also the age of legal adulthood. It is the noun built on maior, not a synonym of major.
entries.definitionCN: 多数、较大部分；也指法定成年年龄。它是建立在 maior 上的名词，不是 major 的同义词。

entries.definition: the elected head of a city. It came through French maire from Latin maior 'greater, chief', so it is a cousin, not a derivative of English major.
entries.definitionCN: 民选市长。它经法语 maire 来自拉丁语 maior“更大、首领”，因此是远亲，而不是英语 major 的派生词。

entries.definition: grand and impressive in appearance. It comes from majesty, from Latin maiestas, built on the same maior 'greater' stem.
entries.definitionCN: 外观宏伟、威严的。它来自 majesty，再上溯拉丁语 maiestas，同样建立在 maior“更大”的词干上。

entries.definition: largest or most important among several. It is close to major but usually points to one clear leader, as in the main reason.
entries.definitionCN: 在若干者中最大或最重要的。它接近 major，但通常指向一个明确的领头者，如 the main reason。

entries.definition: highest in rank or authority. It stresses position at the top of a hierarchy, while major stresses weight in a comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 位次或权力最高的。它强调层级顶端的位置，而 major 强调比较中的分量。

entries.definition: first in importance, especially of a reason, aim, or sum. It is more formal and narrower than major.
entries.definitionCN: 最重要的，尤用于理由、目标或款项。它比 major 更正式，适用范围更窄。

entries.definition: large or important enough to be noticed or to matter. It can measure degree where major measures rank.
entries.definitionCN: 大到或重要到值得注意、值得当回事。它可量程度，而 major 量位次。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maior is the comparative of magnus, and the same 'great' stem runs through majority, majesty, magnify, magnitude and master.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maior 是 magnus 的比较级，同一条“大”词干贯穿 majority、majesty、magnify、magnitude、master。

normal.en: maior is a comparative, so major always implies 'than the other one'. A major road matters more than a minor road, not because it is wider.
normal.cn: maior 是比较级，所以 major 总隐含“比另一个更……”。主干道比次要道路重要，不是因为它更宽。

normal.en: magnus 'great' gives magnify, magnitude and magnate; maior gives major, majority and majesty. One family, two stems.
normal.cn: magnus“大”给出 magnify、magnitude、magnate；maior 给出 major、majority、majesty。同一个家族，两条词干。

normal.en: The academic major is the subject given the most weight in a degree, which is why the same word also means 'the important one'.
normal.cn: 大学的 major 是学位中分量最重的科目，这也是同一个词又表示“重要的那一个”的原因。

normal.en: A major in the army is the senior officer in a group, and a legal major is the older person across the age line: both are the 'greater' side.
normal.cn: 军队里的 major 是一群军官中资历更高者，法律上的 major 是年龄界线另一侧的年长者：两者都是“更大”的那一侧。

normal.en: Major league and the majors keep the comparison between leagues: the top circuit is the greater one.
normal.cn: major league 与 the majors 保留的是联盟之间的比较：顶级联盟就是“更大”的那一个。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with two pans. Whatever is placed in them, major names the pan that sinks: more weight, more rank, more risk, more volume.
abstract.cn: 想象一架两端有托盘的天平。无论放进去的是什么，major 指的都是下沉的那一盘：更多分量、更高位次、更大风险、更大体量。

abstract.en: The comparison can be held between cities, keys, subjects, officers or leagues; only the scale changes, never the gesture of weighing.
abstract.cn: 比较可以发生在城市、调式、学科、军官或联盟之间；变的只是尺子，称量这个动作从未改变。

abstract.en: Because one pan is already lower, there is no room to add 'very': the comparison is complete before the adjective is spoken.
abstract.cn: 因为有一盘已经更低，“very”就无处可加：比较在形容词出口之前就已经完成了。

examples.en: Lack of sleep was a major factor in the accident.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足是这起事故的一个主要因素。

examples.en: She majored in history and later became a curator.
examples.cn: 她主修历史，后来成了策展人。

examples.en: The symphony ends in a confident major key.
examples.cn: 这首交响曲在一个自信的大调上结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: “梅杰”——梅杰先生主修经济学，后来升为少校 → major 主要的、主修、少校

root: 拉丁语 maior“更大的”，是 magnus“大”的比较级，核心是“两者相比更重、更高的一侧”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of major, all one act of weighing: importance, scale, severity, a musical interval, a chosen subject, an officer's rank, legal age, the top league, and the boundary where the word stops meaning 'big'.
sensesIntro.cn: major 的九个义项都出自同一次称量：重要性、规模、严重程度、音程、主修科目、军衔、法定成年、顶级联盟，以及它不再表示“尺寸大”的用法边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things are weighed, and major names the heavier pan.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西被称量，major 指更重的那一盘。

branches.en: WEIGHT: importance and quantity are the same comparison read on two different scales.
branches.cn: 分量：重要性与数量是同一场比较在两把不同尺子上的读数。

branches.en: SEVERITY: in medicine the heavier side is the higher risk, so the comparison becomes a warning.
branches.cn: 严重性：在医学里更重的一侧就是更高风险，于是比较变成一种警示。

branches.en: INTERVAL: music measures the greater interval on the keyboard, a half-step above the minor.
branches.cn: 音程：音乐在键盘上量出更大的音程，比小调高一个半音。

branches.en: SELECTION: a chosen subject and a top league are both the item given the most weight in a set.
branches.cn: 选择：主修科目与顶级联盟都是在集合中被赋予最大分量的那一项。

branches.en: RANK, AGE AND BOUNDARY: a senior officer and an adult past the legal line are the greater side of a hierarchy, while the last branch marks the point where major stops meaning 'big'.
branches.cn: 位次、年龄与边界：资历更高的军官与越过法定年龄线的成年人是层级中更大的一侧；最后一条标出 major 不再表示“尺寸大”的分界。

intro.en: Major is not built with a living English prefix. Its Latin stem maior is already a comparative; English only adds noun and adverb suffixes to the finished word.
intro.cn: major 不是用活的英语前缀构成的。它的拉丁词干 maior 本身已是比较级；英语只是在成品词后加名词与副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family splits into two stems: magnus 'great' (magnify, magnitude) and its comparative maior 'greater' (major, majority, majesty). They are one root seen from two angles.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族分成两条词干：magnus“大”（magnify、magnitude）及其比较级 maior“更大”（major、majority、majesty）。它们是同一个词根的两个视角。

items.structure: Medieval Latin majoritas, from maior (greater) + -itas (noun of state)
items.meaning: the larger part of a group; the winning number of votes; the age of legal adulthood
items.meaningCN: 多数；多数票；法定成年（-ity 构成状态或性质名词）
items.example: The majority of members voted for the change.
items.exampleCN: 多数成员投票支持这项改变。

items.meaning: extremely, or in a major way (informal)
items.example: I am majorly late for the meeting.

items.meaning: a military officer ranked below a lieutenant general
items.example: A major-general took command of the division.
items.exampleCN: 一位少将接管了这个师。

items.structure: major + domo (from Latin major domus 'chief of the household')
items.meaning: the chief servant managing a large household
items.meaningCN: 大管家；总管（原义“家宅之首”）
items.example: The majordomo greeted the guests at the door.
items.exampleCN: 大管家在门口迎接客人。

items.example: The comparative is the direct source of major.
items.exampleCN: 这个比较级是 major 的直接来源。

items.example: The positive degree stands behind magnify and magnitude.
items.exampleCN: 这个原级支撑 magnify 与 magnitude。

items.example: The stem appears in major, majority and majesty.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 major、majority 与 majesty。

items.example: It forms majority, the greater part.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 majority，即较大部分。

items.meaning: a person of great wealth or power
items.example: A shipping magnate funded the library.
items.exampleCN: 一位航运巨头资助了这座图书馆。

latinEntries.meaning: to make something appear or become greater
greatness of size, importance, or brightness
latinEntries.meaningCN: 巨大；重要性；星等（大小或程度的量）

latinEntries.meaning: a person with control, skill, or authority
latinEntries.meaningCN: 主人；大师；硕士（原指“更甚者、首领”）
威严；陛下（王室尊称，原义“伟大”）

definition_zh: 安静地；轻声地；平静地；不张扬地
definition_en: with little or no noise; in a calm way, without fuss; without attracting public attention
core_image: 一双把门轻轻带上的手，门把转得极慢
scene: 病房里，护士把门轻轻带上，连门把都转得很慢，怕吵醒刚睡着的人。 She quietly closed the door so the patient could sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 quietly 是「安静地、轻声地」（第 1 个义项：几乎不发出声音地做某事）；句意为她轻轻关上门，好让病人能睡。画面里可留意：缓慢转动的门把、病房的走廊灯。

pos.zh: 安静地；轻声地；平静地；不张扬地

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的形容词，指安静的、平静的
quiet 加 -ness，指安静的状态
quiet 加 -en，指使安静下来

senses.title: With little or no noise
senses.definition: making very little sound while doing something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事时几乎不发出声音
senses.example: She closed the door quietly behind her.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻把门在身后关上。
senses.why: The adverb adds the manner ending to the adjective of silence, so it describes an action carried out without noise.
senses.whyCN: 副词在表示寂静的形容词后加上方式词尾，因此描述一个不带声音完成的动作。

senses.title: In a calm way
senses.definition: without showing strong feeling or making a fuss
senses.definitionCN: 不显露强烈情绪、不吵不闹地
senses.example: He quietly accepted the criticism and went back to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静地接受了批评，回去继续工作。
senses.why: Calm of feeling was part of the adjective's meaning, and the adverb carries that stillness into the description of an action.
senses.whyCN: 情绪的平静本就是形容词含义的一部分，副词把这种静止带进了对动作的描述。

senses.title: Without attracting attention
senses.definition: in a way that avoids public notice
senses.definitionCN: 避免引起公众注意地
senses.example: The company quietly expanded while its rivals argued in public.
senses.exampleCN: 对手公开争吵时，这家公司悄然扩张。
senses.why: A person who makes no noise attracts no notice, so the adverb came to describe action done out of sight.
senses.whyCN: 不制造声音的人也不引起注意，于是这个副词转而描述在人们视线之外完成的行动。

intro.en: Quietly is the adjective quiet plus the English adverb ending -ly; its history is the history of quiet.
intro.cn: quietly 是形容词 quiet 加英语副词词尾 -ly；它的历史就是 quiet 的历史。

items.en: The root meant rest, and rest of body, mind and place is the source of every sense.
items.cn: 词根意为休息，身体、心境与地方的休息是一切义项的源头。

items.en: The adjective described someone or something at peace, and English took it through French.
items.cn: 这个形容词形容处于安宁中的人或物，英语经法语把它接受过来。

items.en: Middle English quiet already covered silence, calm and modesty, so the adverb inherited all three.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quiet 已涵盖寂静、平静与低调，副词便继承了这三层意思。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb of manner, telling how an action is done.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成方式副词，说明一个动作是怎样做的。

items.en: Modern English uses quietly for sound, for calm behaviour and for action kept out of public view.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quietly 指声音、举止的平静，以及避开公众视线的行动。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base adjective and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of softness and calm.
note.cn: 形近组收基础形容词及其亲属；近义组收表示轻声与平静的副词。

entries.definition: Making little noise or showing little excitement.
entries.definitionCN: 声音小或不显露兴奋的。

entries.definition: To make or become quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 使安静下来。

entries.definition: The state of being quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 安静的状态。

entries.definition: A literary word for calmness.
entries.definitionCN: 书面语，指宁静、安详。

entries.definition: With a gentle, low sound.
entries.definitionCN: 以轻柔、低沉的声音。

entries.definition: Without making any sound at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全不发出声音地。

entries.definition: In a peaceful, controlled way.
entries.definitionCN: 以平和、克制的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that avoids attracting notice.
entries.definitionCN: 以不惹人注意的方式。

normalIntro.en: The word simply says that an action was done in the manner of quiet: little sound, little fuss, little notice.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只是说，一个动作是以 quiet 的方式完成的：声音少、动静少、惹人注意少。

normal.en: Quietly is quiet plus -ly; if you know the adjective, you already know the adverb.
normal.cn: quietly 就是 quiet 加 -ly；认识形容词，也就认识了这个副词。

normal.en: More quietly and most quietly are the comparatives, because a long adverb prefers more to -er.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more quietly 与 most quietly，因为较长的副词更爱用 more 而不用 -er。

normal.en: Speak quietly is the standard phrase for lowering your voice in a shared room.
normal.cn: speak quietly 是在公共房间里压低声音的标准说法。

normal.en: Quietly confident describes someone sure of themselves without needing to show it.
normal.cn: quietly confident 形容一个人自信却不必表现出来。

normal.en: A thing done quietly is often done well, because it was done without a performance.
normal.cn: 安静做成的事往往做得好，因为它没有被表演化。

abstract.en: The adverb quietly hides its subject: we often hear the result and never the person who acted.
abstract.cn: 副词 quietly 把动作的主语藏了起来：我们常听到结果，却从不知道是谁做的。

abstract.en: Doing something quietly can be a form of respect, and also a form of power.
abstract.cn: 安静地做一件事，既可能是一种尊重，也可能是一种权力。

abstract.en: A culture that praises speaking loudly will still depend on those who work quietly.
abstract.cn: 一个赞美大声表达的文化，仍然依赖那些安静做事的人。

examples.en: He quietly shut the gate so the dog would not bark.
examples.cn: 他悄悄关上院门，免得狗叫起来。

examples.en: She quietly explained the mistake without blaming anyone.
examples.cn: 她平静地解释了这个错误，没有责怪任何人。

examples.en: The village quietly became a favourite place for painters.
examples.cn: 这个村子悄然成了画家们偏爱的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快饿特利」——饿得说话都没力气，只能安安静静，记住 quietly 是安静地。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（安宁的）→ 古法语 quite → 英语 quiet + -ly → quietly；同族有 quietness、quieten。

sensesIntro.en: The core is little sound; the senses extend to calm behaviour and to action kept out of public view.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「声音小」；义项扩展到举止的平静与避开公众视线的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands turning a door handle very slowly so the latch makes no click.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手极慢地转动门把，让锁舌不发出一声轻响。

branches.en: a latch turned without a sound
branches.cn: 无声转动的门锁

branches.en: a voice lowered in a shared room
branches.cn: 公共房间里压低的声音

branches.en: an apology offered without drama
branches.cn: 不带戏码的道歉

branches.en: a new branch opened with no announcement
branches.cn: 没有公告就开张的新分店

branches.en: the same restraint applied to sound and to feeling
branches.cn: 同一种克制，一次用于声音，一次用于情绪

intro.en: The word is the old adjective of rest plus the common adverb ending, so its structure is root, adjective and manner suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示休息的古老形容词加上常见副词词尾，结构为词根、形容词与方式后缀三层。

latinIntro.en: The root reaches English through French, and the adverb adds a native English ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词根经法语进入英语，副词则加上了英语本族的词尾。

definition_zh: 改进；改善；提高；好转
definition_en: to make or become better
core_image: 把一块毛坯石一点点磨亮
scene: 训练日记上写满记录。 Practicing every morning improved his serve.
sceneCN: 这里 improve 是「改进、提高」（第 1 个义项：使更好）；句意：每天早晨的练习提高了他的发球水平。

derivatives.zh: 改进；改善；加名词后缀
改良的；分词转形容词
改进者；改良物

senses.title: To make better
senses.definition: to raise the quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 提升某物的品质
senses.example: The new plan improved the workflow.
senses.exampleCN: 新方案改进了工作流程。
senses.why: A rough stone is ground brighter stroke by stroke.
senses.whyCN: 毛坯石被一刀刀磨亮。

senses.title: To become better
senses.definition: to become better in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 品质或状态变好
senses.example: Her eyesight improved after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后她的视力好转了。
senses.why: The grinding continues even without a hand behind it.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有手在背后，打磨也在继续。

senses.title: To use an opportunity well
senses.definition: to make good use of a chance or time
senses.definitionCN: 好好利用机会或时间
senses.example: He improved the pause to study the menu.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用间歇研究了菜单。
senses.why: Time is a stone too: grind it into something valuable.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是块石头：把它磨成有价值的东西。

senses.title: To raise in value
senses.definition: to increase the worth of land or property
senses.definitionCN: 增加土地或财产的价值
senses.example: They improved the house before selling.
senses.exampleCN: 卖房前他们先翻修了房子。
senses.why: A better stone sells for more; polish adds price.
senses.whyCN: 更好的石头卖价更高；打磨即增值。

intro.en: Improve grew out of the old phrase emprowe, to turn a profit, from Old French prowe, profit or advantage, related to English boot in the old sense of advantage. The business root still lives in the word: to improve is to add gain.
intro.cn: improve 由旧短语 emprowe「获利润」发展而来，出自古法语 prowe「利润、益处」，与英语 boot 的旧义「益处」相关。商业根源仍活在词中：improve 即增益。

items.en: Old French prowe meant profit or advantage, itself from a word for benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 prowe 意为利润或益处，源自表示利益的词。

items.en: The phrase en prou, to one's profit, prefixed the verb emprower.
items.cn: 短语 en prou「于己有利」前缀出动词 emprower。

items.en: Middle English improven first meant to turn land to profit by enclosure.
items.cn: 中古英语 improven 先指圈地使土地产生收益。

items.en: The profit sense widened to making anything better.
items.cn: 利润义扩大为使一切变得更好。

items.en: The nineteenth century standardized improvement in industry, education and health.
items.cn: 十九世纪 improvement 在工业、教育与卫生领域标准化。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the improve family and the false cousin approve. The meaning group compares bettering words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 improve 词族与假表亲 approve；词义组比较表示变好的词。

entries.definition: the act or result of improving.
entries.definitionCN: 改进；改善。本词的名词。

entries.definition: to accept or agree. Looks close but comes from Latin probare, to test.
entries.definitionCN: 批准。字形相近，但源自拉丁语 probare「检验」。

entries.definition: a person or thing that improves.
entries.definitionCN: 改进者。表人后缀形式。

entries.definition: to add value or strength to something good.
entries.definitionCN: 增强。为已有的好加值。

entries.definition: to make finer and more polished.
entries.definitionCN: 精炼。做得更精细更雅。

entries.definition: to move forward toward a better state.
entries.definitionCN: 进步。朝更好状态前进。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split improve into im + prove, reuse the profit root and warn against approve.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 improve 拆成 im 加 prove，复用利润词根，并警示 approve。

normal.en: Old root said profit: to improve is to add gain, not just change.
normal.cn: 旧词根说利润：improve 是增益，不只是改变。

normal.en: improve on takes a base: improve on last year's record.
normal.cn: improve on 带基数：超越去年的纪录。

normal.en: Do not swap improve and approve; one makes better, one says yes.
normal.cn: 不要互换 improve 与 approve：一个变好，一个点头。

normal.en: improvement is the noun box that stores the change.
normal.cn: improvement 是收纳变化的名词盒子。

normal.en: improved marks the finished grind: an improved engine.
normal.cn: improved 标记打磨完成：improved engine。

abstract.en: One image: a dull stone growing a bright edge.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：钝石长出锋刃。

abstract.en: Improvement is profit paid in quality.
abstract.cn: improvement 是以品质支付的利润。

abstract.en: Two directions: you improve things, or things improve themselves.
abstract.cn: 两个方向：你改进事物，或事物自行好转。

examples.en: The software improved greatly after the update.
examples.cn: 更新后软件大有改善。

examples.en: Reading daily will improve your vocabulary.
examples.cn: 每天阅读会提高你的词汇量。

examples.en: The city improved the park with new paths and lights.
examples.cn: 市政府用新步道和路灯升级了公园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一姆普如夫」：一母（一条母线）普普通通，如（入）夫（工厂）打磨就 improve。

root: 古法语 prowe「利润、益处」→ 短语 en prou → emprower「使获利」→ 中古英语 improven「圈地获利」→ 现代英语 improve「改进、好转」；与 approve（拉丁 probare）无同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Improve grinds better: objects, bodies, chances and property all take a brighter edge.
sensesIntro.cn: improve 打磨一切更好：物件、身体、机会与财产都被磨出更亮的光。

core.en: A rough thing gaining value under steady grinding.
core.cn: 毛坯在持续打磨下增值。

branches.en: MAKING: the new plan improved the workflow.
branches.cn: 使动：新方案改进了流程。

branches.en: BECOMING: eyesight improved after the operation.
branches.cn: 自动：术后视力好转。

branches.en: OPPORTUNITY: improving a pause to study.
branches.cn: 机会：利用间隙学习。

branches.en: VALUE: improving a house before selling.
branches.cn: 增值：卖前翻修房屋。

branches.en: TREND: improving steadily, year over year.
branches.cn: 趋势：逐年稳步提升。

intro.en: Improve adds a small family: improvement, improved, improver, with approve as the misleading neighbor.
intro.cn: improve 的词族不大：improvement、improved、improver，旁边还有易误导的 approve。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: the family is French and Anglo-French in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：词族出自法语与盎格鲁-法语。

items.example: The route improved with new signs.
items.exampleCN: 新路牌改善了路线体验。

items.meaning: the act or result of improving
items.example: The improvement showed in the numbers.
An improved model shipped in May.

items.meaning: one who or that which improves
items.example: Steam was a great improver of travel.
items.exampleCN: 蒸汽机大大改进了出行。

items.example: The system is improvable at low cost.

items.exampleCN: 书架上排满自我提升类书。

definition_zh: 神；上帝；神像；极受崇拜的人
definition_en: a being worshipped as having special powers over the world, or a person admired intensely
core_image: 高处的存在：掌控世界、被人仰望敬拜
scene: 古庙里，人们对着神像低头合掌祈愿。 People prayed to their gods at the old temple.
sceneCN: 这里 god 是「神；神像」（第 1 个义项：被敬拜的超自然存在）；句意为人们在古庙向他们的神祈祷。

pos.zh: 神；上帝；神像；偶像般的人物

derivatives.zh: 由 god 加 -ess 构成，义为「女神」
由 god 加 -like 构成，义为「神一般的」
由 god 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚的；神圣的」

senses.title: A being worshipped
senses.definition: a superhuman being or image worshipped as having power over nature
senses.definitionCN: 被敬拜、被认为能左右自然的超人存在或其形象
senses.example: People prayed to their gods at the old temple.
senses.exampleCN: 人们在古庙向他们的神祈祷。
senses.why: The core image is something above humans that controls the world, so the plain sense is the worshipped being.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是凌驾于人、掌控世界的存在，最基本的义项就是被敬拜的对象。

senses.title: God as the one supreme being
senses.definition: the one all-powerful creator, written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 全知全能的唯一造物主，首字母大写
senses.example: She thanks God for her family's safety.
senses.exampleCN: 她感谢上帝保佑全家平安。
senses.why: When many powers shrink to one, the word is raised and capitalized as the single God.
senses.whyCN: 当众神归于一神，词形随之抬升、大写，指唯一的上帝。

senses.title: An image or idol
senses.definition: a carved image treated as a god
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神的雕刻形象
senses.example: The wooden god stood in the shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 木制神像立在神龛里。
senses.why: The invisible being is given a visible body, so the image carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 无形的神被赋予可见的身体，形象便继承了名字。

senses.title: An intensely admired person
senses.definition: a person admired so much that others treat them like a deity
senses.definitionCN: 被崇拜到近乎神明的人
senses.example: Teenagers treated the singer as a pop god.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年把那位歌手当作流行乐之神。
senses.why: Worship keeps its shape even when the object is human, so admired people become gods.
senses.whyCN: 敬拜的形态保留，即使对象换成人，被膜拜的名人便成了 god。

senses.title: A supreme example
senses.definition: something regarded as the ultimate in its kind
senses.definitionCN: 某类事物中的极致代表
senses.example: This bakery is the god of all breakfast shops in town.

definition_zh: 男警察；警员
definition_en: a man who is a member of the police force; a male police officer
core_image: 街角站着一名穿制服的男警，帽檐压得很正，手按在腰间的对讲机上
scene: 路口红灯坏了，车流乱成一团。 A policeman stepped into the crossing and began to wave the cars through.
sceneCN: 这里 policeman 是「男警察」（第 1 个义项：警察队伍里的男性成员）；句意为一名男警察走到斑马线上，开始挥手指挥车辆通行。

senses.title: A male member of the police force
senses.definition: a man whose job is to keep order, enforce the law and help the public as a member of the police
senses.definitionCN: 以维持秩序、执行法律、帮助公众为职业的男性，属于警察队伍
senses.example: A policeman helped the old lady across the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一名男警察扶老太太过了马路。
senses.why: Police names the force as a whole, and man turns it into one person you can point at on the street.
senses.whyCN: police 指整支警察队伍，man 把它落到街上可以指着的一个具体的人身上。

senses.title: A figure of order and help
senses.definition: a person seen as the symbol of law and order, or the one you turn to when there is trouble
senses.definitionCN: 被视为法律与秩序象征的人，或出了事时大家去求助的那个人
senses.example: Every child on the street knows the policeman at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 街上的每个孩子都认识街角那位警察。
senses.why: Because the job is standing in public with authority, the word also names the trusted figure that stands for order, not just the man in uniform.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个职业就是带着权威站在公众面前，这个词也用来指秩序本身的象征，不只是那身制服下的一个人。

intro.en: Policeman is an English compound: police, borrowed through French from a Greek word for the city and its administration, joined to man.
intro.cn: policeman 是英语复合词：police 经法语借自希腊语中表示城市及其行政的词，再与 man 复合。

items.en: Greek polis named a city or city-state, and its affairs: citizenship, administration, public order.
items.cn: 希腊语 polis 指城市或城邦，也指城市的事务：公民身份、行政、公共秩序。

items.en: From polis came politeia, the condition and organization of the citizen body, government of a city.
items.cn: 由 polis 派生出 politeia，指公民共同体的状态与组织方式，即城邦的治理。

items.en: Latin took over politeia as politia, keeping the sense of civil administration and government.
items.cn: 拉丁语吸收了 politeia 作 politia，保留公民行政与治理的含义。

items.en: Old French police meant the ordering and government of a community before it narrowed to the force that keeps order.
items.cn: 古法语 police 先指对共同体的治理与秩序安排，后来才缩小到维持秩序的那支队伍。

items.en: English compounded police with man to make policeman, one identifiable male officer of that force, with the irregular plural policemen.
items.cn: 英语把 police 与 man 复合成 policeman，指这支队伍中一名可以辨认的男性警员，复数为不规则形式 policemen。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the compound family and one word that only echoes the ending; the near-meaning group gathers people of the same calling.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个复合词族的词，另收一个只是词尾相像的词；近义组收同一职业的各类人员。

entries.definition: A person holding a position of authority, often used of police officers.

normalIntro.cn: 这个词是直白的复合词，词族里反复出现同一个两段式画面：一支队伍，加上穿着它的那个人。

normal.en: Police comes from Greek polis, the city, so a policeman is literally a man of the city's order.
normal.cn: police 来自希腊语 polis（城市），所以 policeman 字面上就是「城邦秩序之人」。

normal.en: Police + man, force + person: the compound says the whole force in one man.
normal.cn: police + man，队伍 + 人：这个复合词用一个人代表整支队伍。

normal.en: The plural is irregular: policeman becomes policemen, exactly like man becoming men.
normal.cn: 复数不规则：policeman 变 policemen，与 man 变 men 完全一致。

normal.en: The same pattern gives policewoman, fireman and postman, so once you know one you know the family.
normal.cn: 同样的构词法给出 policewoman、fireman、postman，认识一个就认识一族。

normal.en: Police is collective and takes a plural verb in British English; policeman is a single, countable person.
normal.cn: police 是集合名词，英式英语中常配复数动词；policeman 则是可数的单个人。

abstract.en: A policeman is order given a face: where he stands, the street agrees on the rules.
abstract.cn: 警察是有面孔的秩序：他站在哪里，哪条街就认同规则。

abstract.en: Calling a policeman is turning private fear into public procedure.
abstract.cn: 叫警察，就是把个人的害怕变成公开的程序。

abstract.en: The uniform erases the person and leaves only the order he carries.
abstract.cn: 制服抹掉个人，只留下他所携带的秩序。

examples.en: A policeman helped the old lady across the road.
examples.cn: 一名男警察扶老太太过了马路。

examples.en: The policemen on patrol found the lost child in the park.
examples.cn: 巡逻的警察们在公园里找到了走失的孩子。

examples.en: If you lose your way at night, ask a policeman for directions.
examples.cn: 晚上迷路的话，向警察问路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡里·死人没」——警察一来，坡里街巷盗贼绝迹，「死人没」这么安全的街道靠的就是 policeman。

root: policeman 由 police 与 man 复合而成；police 经古法语 police（公共行政、秩序）上溯拉丁语 politia，最终源自希腊语 polis（城邦），与 policy 同源但词义早已分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The compound takes a whole force and puts it into one street-level person; the senses run from the man in uniform to the idea of order he stands for.
sensesIntro.cn: 复合词把整支队伍装进一个街头层面的人身上；义项从穿制服的那个人，走到他所代表的秩序观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man in uniform at a street corner, his hand on the crossing signal.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角穿制服的男人，手按在路口的指挥信号上。

branches.en: a man waving cars through a broken crossing
branches.cn: 在失灵路口挥手放行车辆的男人

branches.en: children greeting the officer at the corner

branches.en: trouble dissolving when the uniform appears
branches.cn: 制服一出现，麻烦就散了

branches.en: a lost child led by the hand to the station
branches.cn: 走失的孩子被牵着手领到警局

branches.en: policemen patrolling the night streets
branches.cn: 夜间巡逻的警察们

intro.en: The compound is English-made, but its first half carries a Greek word for the city all the way through French and Latin.
intro.cn: 复合词本身是英语造的，但前一半带着一个希腊语的「城邦」词，一路经过法语和拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The Greek politeia passed into Latin as politia; that Latin form is the recorded carrier of the word into Romance, so it is listed as the linking entry.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 politeia 进入拉丁语作 politia；这个拉丁形式是该词进入罗曼语族的记录载体，列为承转条目。

definition_zh: 保护；防护；保障；为（文件等）设置保护
definition_en: to keep a person or thing safe from harm, damage or loss, whether by covering it, by guarding it in law and insurance, or by locking it behind a password
core_image: 一个人张开外套挡在孩子身前，雨点全落在那层布上
scene: 暴雨来得突然，母亲把外套撑开罩住孩子，自己的后背全湿了。 She held her coat over the boy to protect him from the downpour.
sceneCN: 这里表示「保护、使不受伤害」（第 1 个义项：用身体或物件挡住危险）；句意为她把外套罩在男孩头上，替他挡住倾盆大雨。

collocations.phrase: protect a file with a password

derivatives.zh: 由 protect 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「保护；防护物」
由 protect 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「保护的；防护的」
由 protect 加表示施动者的 -or 构成，义为「保护者；保护装置」
由 protect 加否定前缀 un- 与过去分词词尾构成，义为「未受保护的」

senses.title: To keep someone safe from harm
senses.definition: to put a person or thing out of reach of harm or damage, usually by placing your body or an object between them and the threat
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物挡在伤害够不到的地方，通常以身体或物件横在人与威胁之间
senses.example: He raised his arm to protect the child from the flying glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他抬起手臂，替孩子挡住飞来的玻璃。
senses.why: Latin protegere joins pro-, in front, with tegere, to cover, so the first picture is a layer held on the side where the blow lands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 protegere 由 pro-（在前面）与 tegere（盖住）合成，最早的动作就是把一层遮盖挡在挨打的那一侧。

senses.title: To guard against a danger that cannot be touched
senses.definition: to take measures that stop disease, cold, rust or an attack from doing damage, even when the danger has no shape you can see
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施阻止疾病、寒冷、锈蚀或攻击造成损害，即使这种危险看不见形迹
senses.example: A thin film of oil protects the blade against rust.
senses.exampleCN: 薄薄一层油能防止刀身生锈。
senses.why: A cover works because anything reaching the surface is stopped there, so English moves the same verb from visible blows to frost, germs and rust, which also arrive from outside.
senses.whyCN: 遮盖之所以有效，是因为凡是够到表面的东西都被拦在那里；于是英语把这个动词从看得见的打击挪到霜冻、病菌和锈蚀上——它们同样来自外面。

senses.title: To secure a right or a possession by law or contract
senses.definition: to use laws, rules or insurance so that a person's rights, property or income cannot easily be taken away or lost
senses.definitionCN: 借助法律、规则或保险，使某人的权利、财产或收入不易被夺走或损失
senses.example: The new clause protects tenants from sudden eviction.
senses.exampleCN: 新条款保障租客不被突然赶走。
senses.why: Law and insurance do for a person's interests what a coat does for the body: they set an enforceable barrier in front of something valuable.
senses.whyCN: 法律与保险对人利益的用处，就跟外套对身体的用处一样：在贵重的东西前面立起一道能强制执行的屏障。

senses.title: To restrict who may open a file or device
senses.definition: to keep a file, account or device from being opened or changed by anyone who has not been allowed in
senses.definitionCN: 使文件、账户或设备不能被未获许可的人打开或改动
senses.example: She protected the folder with a password before lending the laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 把电脑借出去之前，她先用密码保护了那个文件夹。
senses.why: A password is the newest form of the same cover: it stands at the door of the file, and only those who know it may lift the cover.
senses.whyCN: 密码是这层遮盖最新的形态：它守在文件门口，只有知道它的人才被允许把遮盖掀开。

intro.en: Protect comes from a Latin verb that meant to cover something on its front side, and that covering later hardened into a legal and then a digital barrier.
intro.cn: protect 来自一个意为「在正面盖住」的拉丁动词；这层遮盖后来变硬，先成为法律屏障，再成为数字屏障。

items.en: Tegere meant to cover or to clothe, and it supplied the covering half of the word.
items.cn: tegere 意为覆盖、遮盖，是这个词里「盖住」的那一半。

items.en: Pro- put the covering in front, so protegere meant to hold something over a person and keep harm away.
items.cn: pro- 把遮盖物放到前面，于是 protegere 意为把某物罩在人身上，把伤害挡开。

items.en: The participle protectus described someone already sheltered, and English borrowed exactly this form rather than the plain verb.
items.cn: 分词 protectus 描述已经被遮护住的人，英语借的正是这个形式，而不是光秃秃的动词。

items.en: Protectio named the act of covering and defending, and through French it became the English noun protection.
items.cn: protectio 指遮盖与防卫的行为，经法语演变成英语名词 protection。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century and widened it from a physical cover to legal guarantees and finally to passwords.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个动词，把「物理遮盖」扩展到法律保障，最后又扩展到密码。

note.en: The first group is built on the Latin verb for covering, with one word that only shares the prefix and the opening letters; the second group gathers verbs for keeping something safe.
note.cn: 第一组建立在表示「遮盖」的拉丁动词上，其中一个词只共用前缀和开头几个字母；第二组收表示「使免受伤害」的动词。

entries.definition: Serving to keep someone or something safe from harm.
entries.definitionCN: 起保护作用的；防护的。

entries.definition: The act of uncovering something hidden, literally the removal of a cover.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏之物；字面义是「把盖子揭掉」。

entries.definition: A natural covering such as skin or a shell; a technical word that keeps the bare sense of covering.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤、外壳等天然覆盖物；专业用语，保留「覆盖」的本义。

entries.definition: A public expression of disagreement; it shares the prefix pro- and the first letters only, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表达反对；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To ward off an attack, often with force or with argument.
entries.definitionCN: 击退攻击，常靠武力或言辞。

entries.definition: To watch over someone or something in order to prevent danger.
entries.definitionCN: 看守某人某物以防范危险。

entries.definition: To put something solid between a person and a threat.
entries.definitionCN: 把实体挡在人与威胁之间。

entries.definition: To protect something important through careful rules or measures.
entries.definitionCN: 通过周密的规定或措施保护重要之物。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps one picture: a cover held on the side the blow comes from, whether the blow is rain, rust, a lawsuit or a stranger at a keyboard.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词始终保留一幅画面：遮盖挡在打击来的那一侧，不管打击是雨、锈、官司，还是键盘那端的陌生人。

normal.en: Pro- means in front and tegere means to cover, so protect is literally to cover something on its front.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前面」，tegere 意为「盖住」，所以 protect 字面上就是「在正面盖住」。

normal.en: Detect turns the picture around: de- takes the cover away, so to detect is to uncover what was hidden.
normal.cn: detect 把这幅画反过来：de- 把盖子拿走，所以 detect 是揭开被藏着的东西。

normal.en: Protection is the noun of the covering, protector is the person who holds it, and protective is the quality of being able to hold it.
normal.cn: protection 是这层遮盖的名词，protector 是举着它的人，protective 是能举得起它的性质。

normal.en: Unprotected adds un- to the participle, so an unprotected wire is simply a wire with no cover in front of it.
normal.cn: unprotected 在分词前加 un-，所以 unprotected wire 就是前面没有任何遮盖的电线。

normal.en: Protect looks like prove because both begin with pro-, but prove goes back to probare, to test, and has no cover in it at all.
normal.cn: protect 与 prove 都以 pro- 开头，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），里面根本没有「盖住」这层意思。

abstract.en: A cover only works while it stays on the side facing the danger, which is why protection is always directed outward.
abstract.cn: 遮盖只有留在朝向危险的那一侧才有效，所以保护总是指向外面。

abstract.en: One verb holds a child, a blade, a tenant and a file because all four can be harmed by something arriving from outside.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词能护住孩子、刀身、租客和文件，因为这四者都可能被从外面来的东西伤到。

abstract.en: To protect is to lend something of your own, a coat, a law or a password, to stand between another person and harm.
abstract.cn: 保护就是把自己的一件东西——外套、法律或密码——借出去，挡在别人与伤害之间。

examples.en: She held her coat over the boy to protect him from the downpour.
examples.cn: 她把外套罩在男孩头上，替他挡住倾盆大雨。

examples.en: These rules protect tenants from sudden eviction.
examples.cn: 这些规定保障租客不被突然赶走。

examples.en: The folder was protected with a password.
examples.cn: 那个文件夹已用密码保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑坦克」——读音近似「扑-坦克」，人扑过去挡在坦克前面，只为护住身后的人；记住 protect 是保护。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前面）+ tegere（盖、遮）→ protegere（在前面遮住、护住）→ protectus（被护住的），十五世纪进入英语。同族词 detect（de- 去掉 + tegere 盖，即揭开盖子）、tegument（覆盖物）都保留「盖」的画面。注意 protect 与 prove 都以 pro- 开头，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验、证实），两者只是前缀相同，词根完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a cover held on the front side; the senses spread from shielding a body to blocking invisible threats, to legal guarantees, and finally to a password at the door of a file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「挡在正面的那层遮盖」；义项从护住身体，扩展到拦住看不见的危险，再到法律保障，最后到文件门口的那道密码。

core.cn: 核心意象：一件外套在孩子身前撑开，雨点全打在那层布上。

branches.cn: 薄油涂在刀身上

intro.cn: 表示覆盖的拉丁动词、把它推到前面的前缀，以及造出名词与形容词的两个英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Tegere and protegere with their participles are the reliable Latin cognates, and the bare root teg- still shows in detect and tegument.
latinIntro.cn: tegere、protegere 及其分词是可靠的同源词；光秃秃的词根 teg- 至今还能在 detect 与 tegument 里看到。
