scene: 朋友劝他别去山上，他笑着答应着，脚下还是往山路走。 He set out for the summit though the clouds were closing in.
sceneCN: 这里 though 是「虽然、尽管」（第 1 个义项：让步从属连词）；句意为尽管乌云正在合拢，他还是出发去山顶了。

pos.zh: 虽然；尽管（引导让步状语从句）

collocations.zh: 与 though 用法相当的 although

derivatives.zh: 由 all 与 though 合成的连词，义为「虽然；尽管」
though 在网络与口语中的简写形式，义同「虽然」

senses.title: In spite of the fact that
senses.definition: used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement surprising or contrasting
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出一个使主句显得意外或形成对照的事实
senses.example: Though the road was steep, they reached the top before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 虽然山路陡峭，他们还是在中午前到达山顶。
senses.why: The word began as the same form as that, and grew into a marker that sets one clause against another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初与 that 同形，后来演变成把一个分句与另一个分句对立起来的标记。

senses.title: However, at the end of a clause
senses.definition: placed at the end of a sentence to add a softer however or a second thought
senses.definitionCN: 放在句末，补充一个语气较软的「不过」或事后想法
senses.example: It is a small flat. Very cosy, though.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一套小公寓，不过很温馨。
senses.why: The contrast marker drifts to the end of the sentence, where it sounds like a spoken afterthought.
senses.whyCN: 这个转折标记漂到句末，听起来像说话人事后补上的念头。

senses.title: As if, in as though
senses.definition: in the phrase as though, meaning as if, used for an imagined situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 as though，意为「好像」，表示设想的情形
senses.example: He spoke as though he had known her for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话的样子好像已经认识她多年。
senses.why: Comparison and concession share one marker: a clause that does not quite match the main one.
senses.whyCN: 比较与让步共用一个标记：一个与主句并不完全相符的分句。

senses.title: Even though: a stronger concession
senses.definition: in the phrase even though, introducing a fact that does not change the result
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 even though，引出一个并不改变结果的事实
senses.example: Even though the shop was closed, a light still burned inside.
senses.exampleCN: 即使店铺已经关门，里面仍亮着灯。
senses.why: Adding even pushes the contrast to its limit: the fact is granted in full and the main clause still stands.
senses.whyCN: 加上 even 把对立推到极限：事实被完全承认，主句依然成立。

intro.en: Though is a native English word built on the old demonstrative stem, a close relative of that.
intro.cn: though 是英语本土词，建立在古老的指示词干之上，与 that 是近亲。

items.en: The Germanic demonstrative stem *þa- supplied words for pointing at something, including then and there.
items.cn: 日耳曼语指示词干 *þa- 提供了一批指称某物的词，包括 then 与 there。

items.en: Old English þeah was both a concessive conjunction and an adverb meaning nevertheless.
items.cn: 古英语 þeah 既是让步连词，也作副词表示「然而」。

items.en: Middle English spelling settled toward though, and the word kept both jobs, conjunction and sentence-final adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写逐渐定为 though，这个词保留了两个用途：连词与句末副词。

items.en: The compound although, formed with all, became the more formal written choice, while though stayed common in speech.
items.cn: 由 all 构成的 although 成为更正式的书面选择，though 则在口语中保持常用。

items.en: As though and even though fixed the two special uses, comparison and reinforced concession.
items.cn: as though 与 even though 固定了两个专门用法：比拟与强化让步。

note.en: The first group separates the though family and its easily confused look-alikes; the second compares concessive and contrast words.
note.cn: 第一组区分 though 词族与易混的形近词；第二组比较让步与转折类词。

entries.definition: The formal written variant, all plus though, with the same concessive meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 虽然（all 与 though 复合，更书面）

entries.definition: From one side to the other; it differs by one letter and is often mistyped for though.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；与 though 只差一个字母，常被误打

entries.definition: Complete and careful; another near spelling with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: The past of think and a noun for an idea; it shares the th opening only.
entries.definitionCN: think 的过去式；只是开头字母相同，词源不同

entries.definition: An adverb of contrast that can start a sentence; stronger and more formal than final though.
entries.definitionCN: 然而（可置于句首，比句末 though 更正式）

entries.definition: In spite of that; a strongly formal contrast adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 然而；尽管如此（正式书面语）

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, especially in formal and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 而；然而（多用于正式与法律文本）

entries.definition: In spite of what has been said; a spoken contrast phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 即便如此（口语转折短语）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the real word family and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自真实词族，以及这个词实际出现的固定短语。

normal.en: Although is all plus though, and it is the cooler, more written version.
normal.cn: although 就是 all 加 though，是更冷静、更书面的版本。

normal.en: As though is the same as as if: a scene that is only imagined.
normal.cn: as though 等于 as if：一个只是想象出来的场景。

normal.en: Even though grants the fact completely, then lets the main clause stand.
normal.cn: even though 先把事实完全承认，再让主句依然成立。

normal.en: Though at the end is a spoken afterthought, like a shrug after a sentence.
normal.cn: 句末的 though 是口语里的补充，像说完一句话后耸耸肩。

normal.en: Though is not through or thought: check the vowel and the ending before writing.
normal.cn: though 不是 through 也不是 thought：下笔前看清元音和结尾。

abstract.en: Picture a road sign that points forward and then bends: the main clause moves on, the concessive clause bends away.
abstract.cn: 想象一块指向前方又突然拐弯的路牌：主句继续前进，让步从句拐向一旁。

abstract.en: Though is the small hinge on which two opposite facts swing.
abstract.cn: though 是让两个相反事实摆动的那个小铰链。

abstract.en: The word nods at one fact and keeps walking toward the other.
abstract.cn: 这个词对一个事实点点头，然后继续走向另一个。

examples.en: Though she was tired, she finished the report that night.
examples.cn: 虽然很累，她当晚还是写完了报告。

examples.en: The soup was simple. It tasted good, though.
examples.cn: 汤很简单，不过味道不错。

examples.en: He looked as though he had seen a ghost.
examples.cn: 他看上去好像见了鬼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「豆」——嘴上说豆子好，转身把豆子推开 → though 虽然

root: 英语本土词，源自古英语 þeah，建立在日耳曼指示词干 *þa-（与 that、then 同源）之上；古英语中兼作让步连词与副词「然而」，后由 all + though 合成更书面的 although。

sensesIntro.en: All four uses of though mark a mismatch: a fact that does not stop the main clause, an afterthought at the end, an imagined comparison, and a concession pushed to its limit.
sensesIntro.cn: though 的四种用法都在标记「不相符」：挡不住主句的事实、句末的补充、设想中的比拟，以及推到极限的让步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence that nods at one fact and then turns its head to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话先对一个事实点头，再扭头转向另一个事实。

branches.en: The standard concession: the fact is granted, the main clause still stands.
branches.cn: 标准让步线：事实被承认，主句依然成立。

branches.en: The spoken tail: contrast dropped at the end like an afterthought.
branches.cn: 口语尾音线：转折被丢到句末，像事后想起。

branches.en: The imagined scene: as though lines up a picture with reality.
branches.cn: 想象场景线：as though 把一幅画面与现实并列。

branches.en: The limit: even though grants everything and still holds.
branches.cn: 极限线：even though 全部承认之后依然成立。

branches.en: Written and spoken halves of the same hinge word.
branches.cn: 同一个铰链词的书面与口语两半。

intro.en: Though is a bare native word; its relatives come from compounds and spellings rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: though 是没有词缀的本土词，它的亲属来自复合与拼写变体，而非后缀。

definition_zh: 原料；配料；要素
definition_en: one of the foods or things that are combined to make something
core_image: 案板上摆开的一排待下锅的材料
scene: 妈妈把鸡蛋、面粉和糖依次排开。 Flour is the main ingredient of bread.
sceneCN: 这里 ingredient 是「原料」（第 1 个义项：混合物的组成部分）；句意：面粉是面包的主要原料。

derivatives.zh: 罕见同源词，义为「共同成分」（极罕用）

senses.title: A food that goes into a dish
senses.definition: one of the foods used to make a dish
senses.definitionCN: 做菜所用食材之一
senses.example: Add the other ingredients slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 慢慢加入其余配料。
senses.why: Each item waits on the board before the pot.

senses.title: A part of a mixture or medicine
senses.definition: one substance in a mixture or product
senses.definitionCN: 混合物或产品中的一种物质

senses.exampleCN: 有效成分镇痛。
senses.why: One powder inside the pill does the work.

senses.title: A quality needed for a result

intro.en: Ingredient is the present participle of Latin ingredi, to step into or enter, from in- (into) and gradi (to step). Each ingredient is something that steps into the pot.
intro.cn: ingredient 是拉丁语 ingredi「走入」的现在分词，由 in-「进入」+ gradi「迈步」构成；每种配料都是走进锅里的东西。

items.en: Latin gradi meant to step, to walk; gradi gave grade and gradual.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradi 意为迈步；同根词有 grade 与 gradual。

items.en: in- plus gradi formed ingredi: to step into, to enter.
items.cn: in- 加 gradi 构成 ingredi：走入、进入。

items.en: ingrediens described a thing stepping in as part of a whole.
items.cn: ingrediens 描述正走入整体之内的事物。

items.en: Medieval Latin ingredientem named a component in medicine and alchemy.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 ingredientem 指医药与炼金中的成分。

items.en: English kept the kitchen sense and added the quality sense.
items.cn: 现代英语保留厨房义，并增加品质义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the step-root family. The meaning group compares words of parts and components.
note.cn: 形近组收录「迈步」词根词族；词义组比较表示组成部分的词。

definition_zh: 历史；历史学；一段过往经历；病史；（事物的）沿革记录
definition_en: the study, record or remembered account of past events, especially of human affairs
core_image: 一间档案室里，纸页按年份排成长排，窗外的街景却在不断变化
scene: 考古队在城墙下挖出层叠的灶台与钱币，这些遗存让这座城的记载提前了三百年，改写本地历史。 The excavation team found stacked hearths and coins beneath the city wall, remains that pushed the town's written record back three centuries and rewrote its history.
sceneCN: 这里 history 指「关于过去事件的记载与叙述」（第 1 个义项：对过往的系统记录）；句意为考古队在城墙下挖出层叠灶台与钱币，这些遗存让该城记载提前三百年，改写了本地历史。可辨识物件：层叠灶台、古钱币、城墙剖面、年份标签。

pos.zh: 历史；历史学；经历；病史（可数指一段经历或一部史书）

derivatives.zh: 历史学家
有历史意义的；历史性的
历史的；史学的

senses.title: The recorded past of human affairs
senses.titleCN: 对人类过往的系统记录
senses.definition: the whole body of past events as recorded, especially those of people and societies
senses.definitionCN: 被记录下来的全部过往事件，尤其是人与社会的经历
senses.example: The town's history begins with a ferry crossing and a salt tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城的历史始于一处渡口和一笔盐税。
senses.why: the Greek word meant inquiry, so history is first the result of asking, then the record that answers.
senses.whyCN: 希腊原词意为「探究」，因此 history 先是提问的结果，再是回答这问题的记录。

senses.title: The discipline that studies the past
senses.definition: the academic discipline that selects, checks and interprets evidence about the past
senses.definitionCN: 选择、核验并解释过去证据的学术学科
senses.example: History became a university subject with its own methods in the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学在 19 世纪成为拥有自身方法的大学学科。
senses.why: once inquiry acquired rules of evidence and training, the word named a profession as well as a record.
senses.whyCN: 当探究有了证据规则与训练体系，这个词就既指记录，也指一门专业。

senses.title: A written narrative of events
senses.definition: a book or account that arranges past events into an ordered narrative
senses.definitionCN: 把过往事件编排为有序叙述的书或记述
senses.example: She wrote a history of the harbour that reads like a novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一部读起来像小说的港口史。
senses.why: the oldest English sense was simply 'a story', and a written history is still a shaped narrative.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的义项就是「故事」，而一部史书至今仍是被塑形的叙述。

senses.title: A person's or thing's past course
senses.definition: the sequence of events that led to someone's or something's present condition
senses.definitionCN: 导致某人或某物当前状况的一系列过往事件
senses.example: The building has a history of leaks and repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼有一连串漏水和修补的经历。
senses.why: the word scales down from whole societies to a single object, because any object also has a course of events.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从整个社会缩小到单个物件，因为任何物件也都有自己的事件序列。

senses.title: A patient's medical record
senses.definition: the record of a person's past illnesses, treatments and family conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某人既往疾病、治疗与家族情况的记录
senses.example: The doctor asked about his family history of heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 医生询问他家族的心脏病史。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the word for the case narrative a doctor takes down, in the same sense of an ordered past.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用这个词指医生记下的病例叙述，仍是「有序的过去」这一层意思。

senses.title: Natural history
senses.definition: the study and record of plants, animals and minerals, including their deep past
senses.definitionCN: 对植物、动物与矿物的研究与记录，包括其深远过去
senses.example: Natural history museums preserve specimens that document extinct species.
senses.exampleCN: 自然史博物馆保存着记录已灭绝物种的标本。
senses.why: the phrase was extended from human affairs to living things once naturalists began recording change over time.
senses.whyCN: 当博物学者开始记录随时间发生的变化，这个短语便从人类事务扩展到生物。

senses.title: A track record of performance
senses.definition: the known record of how something has performed, used to judge what it will do next
senses.definitionCN: 某事物以往表现的已知记录，用以判断其下一步表现
senses.example: The fund has a history of steady returns in bad years.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金在坏年份里有着稳定回报的往绩。
senses.why: the commercial use treats the past as evidence for the future, which is the same logic as historical inference.
senses.whyCN: 商业用法把过去当作未来的证据，这与史学推论是同一套逻辑。

senses.title: Abstract: the remembered past itself
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：被记忆的过去本身
senses.definition: the past as it is remembered, contested and used by a community in the present
senses.definitionCN: 被当下群体记忆、争夺与使用的那个过去
senses.example: The two villages tell different histories of the same flood.
senses.exampleCN: 两个村庄对同一场洪水讲述着不同的历史。
senses.why: the abstract use stresses that history is carried and argued over, not merely stored.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法强调历史是被携带、被争辩的，而不只是被存放的。

intro.en: History comes from Greek historia 'inquiry, knowledge gained by inquiry', from histor 'one who knows, witness', generally linked to idein 'to see'. It entered English through Latin and French, first meaning 'story'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: history 来自希腊 historia「探究、经由探究所得的知识」，其词源 histor 意为「知情者、见证人」，一般与 idein「看见」相联系。它经拉丁语与法语进入英语，最初意为「故事」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Histor meant 'witness, one who knows'; it is generally taken to continue a root meaning 'to see, to know', the same root behind English wit.
items.cn: histor 意为「见证人、知情者」；一般被认为延续了表示「看见、知道」的词根，英语 wit 也出于同一词根。

items.en: Historia was 'inquiry, investigation, the knowledge so gained', the word Herodotus used for his own research.
items.cn: historia 意为「探究、调查及由此获得的知识」，希罗多德就用这个词称呼自己的研究。

items.en: Latin historia kept both the inquiry and the written account, and the account sense grew stronger in later use.
items.cn: 拉丁 historia 同时保留「探究」与「成文记述」，在后世用法中记述义渐强。

items.en: Old French historie brought the word into English in the thirteenth century as 'a story, a narrative', whether true or not.
items.cn: 古法语 historie 于 13 世纪把词带入英语，意为「故事、叙述」，无论真假。

items.en: By the nineteenth century history meant the professional study of past societies, with archives, seminars and source criticism.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，history 指对过往社会的专业研究，配有档案、研讨课与史料批判。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact date when 'the past events themselves' replaced 'a story' as the dominant sense is not fixed, so the chronology given here is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：泛指「过去事件本身」取代「故事」成为主要义项的确切年代尚无定论，此处给出的时间线为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like history but name a different thing; group two holds the forms in which the past is written down.
note.cn: 第一组是外形像 history、却指别的事物的词；第二组是过去被书写下来的形态。

entries.definition: From Old French estorie, the same source as history: a narrative that may be true or invented, which is exactly what history once meant.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 estorie，与 history 同源：可真可虚构的叙述，而这正是 history 最初的义项。

entries.definition: An adjective for an event important enough to enter history, not for anything old or past.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指重要到足以载入史册的事件，而非任何古老或过去之物。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning connected with past events or with the study of them, the neutral partner of history.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为与过去事件或史学研究有关，是 history 的中性搭配词。

entries.definition: The study of how histories are written, not the events themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 研究历史如何被书写，而不是研究事件本身。

entries.definition: From Greek chronos 'time': a record arranged strictly by date, with less interpretation than a history.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 chronos「时间」：严格按日期排列的记录，解释成分少于 history。

entries.definition: The raw stored evidence, such as files and registers; history is the interpretation built on such records.
entries.definitionCN: 被保存的原始证据，如档案与登记册；history 是在这些记录之上建立的解释。

entries.definition: All that has happened; history is the part that has been selected, recorded and interpreted.
entries.definitionCN: 一切已发生之事；history 只是其中被选择、记录与解释的部分。

entries.definition: The stored documents and the place holding them; they are the raw material, not the account.
entries.definitionCN: 被保存的文件与存放它们的场所；它们是原料，不是叙述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek historia means inquiry, so history is knowledge obtained by asking questions of evidence.
normal.cn: 希腊 historia 意为探究，所以 history 是通过追问证据获得的知识。

normal.en: Histor is the witness, one who knows, linked to the root for seeing.
normal.cn: histor 是见证人、知情者，与表示「看见」的词根相联系。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was story, which is why a history can still be told as a narrative.
normal.cn: 英语最早义项是 story，所以一部历史至今仍可作为叙述来讲。

normal.en: Keep historic and historical apart: one means momentous, the other means relating to the past.
normal.cn: 把 historic 与 historical 分开：一个指重大，一个指与过去有关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: oral history, medical history, natural history.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分支：口述史、病史、自然史。

abstract.en: Picture shelves of paper ordered by year while the street outside keeps changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一排按年份排好的纸页，而窗外的街道不断变化。

abstract.en: Picture two villages telling the same flood in two different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象两个村庄用两种说法讲述同一场洪水。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger whose columns are evidence and whose margin is argument.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，栏目是证据，页边是争论。

examples.en: The excavation rewrote the town's history and doubled its recorded age.
examples.cn: 这次发掘改写了这座城的历史，使其有记载的年代翻了一倍。

examples.en: History is taught as a set of arguments about evidence, not as a list of dates.
examples.cn: 历史被作为一组关于证据的论证来教授，而不是一串日期。

examples.en: The fund's history of steady returns attracted cautious investors.
examples.cn: 这只基金稳定回报的往绩吸引了谨慎的投资者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「his（他的）+ story（故事）」——他的故事写成书 → 历史

root: 希腊 historia「探究、探究所得的知识」，出自 histor「见证人、知情者」，一般与 idein「看见」同根，再往上与印欧词根「看见、知道」相联系；英语 history 经拉丁 historia 与古法语 historie。更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one word from the recorded past to the discipline, the written book, a personal course, a medical file, the natural world, a track record and finally the past as memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个词展开：从被记录的过去，到学科、史书、个人经历、病历、自然界、往绩，最后是作为记忆的过去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: papers ordered by year in a room while the street outside changes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一室之内纸页按年排好，窗外街景却在变化。

branches.en: ASK AND WRITE: inquiry produces a record, and the record takes narrative shape.
branches.cn: 追问与书写：探究产生记录，记录又成为叙述。

branches.en: PROFESSION: once evidence has rules, the word names a discipline and its training.
branches.cn: 职业：证据一旦有了规则，这个词就指一门学科及其训练。

branches.en: SMALLER COURSES: a building or a fund also has a sequence that can be told and judged.
branches.cn: 更小的历程：一栋楼或一只基金同样有可被讲述与评判的序列。

branches.en: BORROWED FIELDS: medicine and natural science keep the same ordered-past logic.
branches.cn: 借用的领域：医学与自然科学保留了同一套「有序过去」逻辑。

branches.en: CONTESTED MEMORY: the past is carried and argued over, not merely shelved.
branches.cn: 被争辩的记忆：过去是被携带与争论的，不只是被束之高阁。

intro.en: History is a Greek noun in English dress; its root and endings also build historian, historic and historiography.
intro.cn: history 是披着英语外衣的希腊名词；其词根与词尾还构成 historian、historic 与 historiography。

latinIntro.en: Latin historia gives history, historian and historiography; Greek histor and the ending -ia are the building blocks.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 historia 构成 history、historian 与 historiography；希腊 histor 与词尾 -ia 是构件。

items.example: The root names the one who was there.
Historia was the title of the first prose inquiry.
items.exampleCN: historia 是第一部散文探究的标题。

items.example: history is historia in English form.
items.exampleCN: history 就是 historia 的英语形态。
那次签署具有历史意义。

items.meaning: of the past or of history

items.example: Historically, the river flooded each spring.
items.exampleCN: 历史上这条河每年春天泛滥。

items.example: Historiography studies how accounts are made.
items.exampleCN: 编史学研究所史如何被写成。

items.example: Prehistoric tools lay in the cave.

definition_zh: 键盘；（乐器的）键盘；用键盘输入
definition_en: the set of keys on a computer, typewriter, or musical instrument, or to enter data using such keys
core_image: 一整片排列整齐的方键，中间那行有一条微微磨亮的横道
scene: 深夜书桌前，屏幕的光照着摊开的双手，指尖在方格里起落。 He wiped crumbs off the keyboard before starting work.
sceneCN: 这里 keyboard 是「键盘」（第 1 个义项：电脑或打字机上的一整排按键），句意为他开始工作前把键盘上的碎屑擦掉。画面里的物件：书桌、屏幕光、双手。

derivatives.zh: 由 keyboard 加 -ist 构成，指键盘手
由 keyboard 加 -ing 构成，指键盘录入技能
构成词根，指单个按键或钥匙

senses.title: The keys of a computer
senses.definition: the set of letter, number, and function keys used to enter data
senses.definitionCN: 用来输入数据的字母、数字和功能键的总和
senses.example: The laptop keyboard is smaller than a desk one.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本键盘比台式机的要小。
senses.why: The panel sense is the base layer: keys set into one board.
senses.whyCN: 面板义是基础层：按键装在同一块板上。

senses.title: The keys of a musical instrument
senses.definition: the row of black and white keys on a piano, organ, or synthesizer
senses.definitionCN: 钢琴、风琴或电子琴上的黑白琴键
senses.example: She learned the piano before she touched a keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 她在弹电子琴之前先学了钢琴。
senses.why: Organs and pianos put the same board of keys under the hands.
senses.whyCN: 风琴和钢琴把同样的一块键板放在手下。

senses.title: An electronic instrument
senses.definition: an electronic instrument played with keys, especially in a band
senses.definitionCN: 用键盘演奏的电子乐器，尤指乐队里的那种
senses.example: The band has drums, bass, and keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队有鼓、贝斯和键盘。
senses.why: An instrument named after its panel is a short step from the panel itself.
senses.whyCN: 以面板命名的乐器，离面板本身只有一步。

senses.title: The typing skill
senses.definition: the skill or activity of typing on a keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 在键盘上打字的技能或活动
senses.example: Keyboarding is taught in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 第一年就教键盘录入。
senses.why: A skill named after the tool shows how central the keyboard became.
senses.whyCN: 以工具命名一项技能，说明键盘有多核心。

senses.title: To enter data by keys
senses.definition: to input text or numbers using a keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 使用键盘输入文字或数字
senses.example: The forms were keyboarded overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这些表格是一夜之间录进去的。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the noun into the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把名词变成使用它的动作。

intro.en: Keyboard is an English compound of key and board, built when keys were set into one panel.
intro.cn: keyboard 是 key 与 board 的英语复合词，在按键被装进同一块面板时才造出来。

items.en: cǣg, key, was the native word for a lock opener.
items.cn: cǣg 是本族词，指开锁的钥匙。

items.en: bord meant a plank, table, or flat surface.
items.cn: bord 意为木板、桌面或平面。

items.en: The compound named the row of keys on an organ in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪时这个复合词指风琴上的琴键排。

items.en: Typewriters carried the word to machines for writing in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪打字机把词义带到书写机器上。

items.en: Computers fixed the modern sense of the panel in front of the screen.
items.cn: 计算机固定了屏幕前那块面板的现代义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the key family; the near-meaning group holds other input and musical terms.
note.cn: 形近组收 key 词族；近义组收其他输入与乐器术语。

entries.definition: One button, or a lock opener.
entries.definitionCN: 构成词根，指单个按键或钥匙。

entries.definition: A small set of keys, as on a phone.
entries.definitionCN: 相似复合词，指电话等的小键盘。

entries.definition: The opening for a key.
entries.definitionCN: 相似复合词，指锁孔。

entries.definition: A machine with keys that prints letters.
entries.definitionCN: 指带键盘的打字机。

entries.definition: A large keyboard instrument with strings.
entries.definitionCN: 指钢琴，键盘乐器的代表。

entries.definition: The display surface next to a keyboard.
entries.definitionCN: 指屏幕，与键盘相邻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks run from a plank with keys to the worn shine on the middle row.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从装着按键的木板走到中间那行磨亮的痕迹。

normal.en: Keyboard is simply key plus board, a board of keys.
normal.cn: keyboard 就是 key 加 board，一块放键的板。

normal.en: Board was the old word for a plank or table.
normal.cn: board 原指木板或桌子。

normal.en: A keyboardist plays the keyboard in a band.
normal.cn: keyboardist 是在乐队里弹键盘的人。

normal.en: Keyboard shortcuts save the fingers a trip to the mouse.
normal.cn: 键盘快捷键让手不必去碰鼠标。

normal.en: The organ had a keyboard before the typewriter did.
normal.cn: 风琴上的键盘比打字机上出现得更早。

abstract.en: A keyboard is a field of small squares you touch in order.
abstract.cn: 键盘是一片要按顺序触碰的小方格。

abstract.en: Every key is a word waiting to be chosen.
abstract.cn: 每个键都是一个等着被选中的字。

abstract.en: The worn middle row shows where thoughts pass most.
abstract.cn: 磨亮的中间一行说明思绪最爱从这里过。

examples.en: She spilled tea on the keyboard again.
examples.cn: 她又把茶洒在键盘上了。

examples.en: The keyboard on this laptop is very quiet.
examples.cn: 这台笔记本的键盘很安静。

examples.en: He keyboarded the whole list in one evening.
examples.cn: 他一晚上把整份清单录了进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ki 板」—— 一块放满了键的板，就是键盘

root: 古英语 cǣg「钥匙」+ bord「木板、桌面」→ 英语复合词 keyboard，十七世纪指风琴键盘，后指打字机与电脑键盘。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: computer keys, instrument keys, the electronic instrument, the typing skill, and the verb for keying data.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：电脑键盘、乐器键盘、电子键盘乐器、键盘录入技能，以及键入数据的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one panel holding a hundred small keys in rows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块面板上成排装着一百来个小键。

branches.en: THE DESK: letters going in and words coming out.
branches.cn: 书桌这条线：字母进去，词出来。

branches.en: THE PIANO: black and white keys in order.
branches.cn: 钢琴这条线：黑白琴键排成行。

branches.en: THE BAND: a player behind two rows of keys.
branches.cn: 乐队这条线：两排键后面的乐手。

branches.en: THE LAPTOP: a small panel folded on a hinge.
branches.cn: 笔记本这条线：折在铰链上的小面板。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: fingers drilled into speed.
branches.cn: 教室这条线：练到熟练的手指。

intro.en: Keyboard is a two-part English compound; the family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: keyboard 是两部分组成的英语复合词，词族靠英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved here, so the list below stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，因此下面留空。

definition_zh: 语法；文法；语法书
definition_en: the set of rules for forming words and sentences in a language, or a book describing them
core_image: 语言背后的规则手册：句子该怎样搭起来
scene: 早读课上，老师把句子成分画成表格贴在黑板上。 The pupil learned grammar rules from the new textbook.
sceneCN: 这里 grammar 是「语法」（第 1 个义项：组词成句的规则系统）；句意为学生从新课本学习语法规则。

derivatives.zh: 由 grammar 加 -ical 构成，义为「合乎语法的」
由 grammatical 加 -ly 构成，义为「在语法上」
由 grammar 加 -ian 构成，义为「语法学家」

senses.title: The rules of a language
senses.definition: the whole system of rules for words and sentences in a language
senses.definitionCN: 一门语言组词成句的整套规则
senses.example: The pupil learned grammar rules from the new textbook.
senses.exampleCN: 学生从新课本学习语法规则。
senses.why: The core image is a hidden manual behind every sentence, so the plain sense is the rule system.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是每个句子背后的隐形手册，最基本的义项就是规则体系。

senses.title: Correct or incorrect use
senses.definition: the degree to which someone speaks or writes correctly
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作符合语法的程度
senses.example: Her grammar improved a lot after one term.
senses.exampleCN: 一学期后她的语法进步很大。
senses.why: The rules can be kept or broken, so the word also measures correctness.
senses.whyCN: 规则可守可破，词义便兼指正确程度。

senses.title: A book of rules
senses.definition: a book that describes the grammar of a language
senses.definitionCN: 描述一门语言语法的书
senses.example: He kept an old grammar on his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他桌上放着一本旧语法书。
senses.why: The rules are printed and bound, so the book borrows the system's name.
senses.whyCN: 规则被印订成册，书便沿用体系之名。

senses.title: The structural system of a field
senses.definition: the basic structure of a subject or art beyond language
senses.definitionCN: 语言之外领域的基本结构
senses.example: The teacher explained the grammar of the dance steps.
senses.exampleCN: 老师讲解了舞步的结构法则。
senses.why: Any craft with fixed rules is said to have its own grammar.
senses.whyCN: 凡有固定规则的技艺都被说成有自己的 grammar。

senses.title: A grammar school tradition
senses.definition: a secondary school historically focused on Latin grammar
senses.definitionCN: 历史上以拉丁语法为核心的中等学校
senses.example: She entered a famous grammar school in town.
senses.exampleCN: 她进了镇上著名的文法学校。
senses.why: Old schools taught grammar above all, so the subject names the school.
senses.whyCN: 旧式学校以语法为纲，学科名便转指学校。

intro.en: Grammar goes back to the Greek art of letters, and glamour is its surprising cousin.
intro.cn: grammar 可追溯到希腊语的「文字之艺」，glamour 是它令人意外的亲戚。

items.en: Greek gramma meant a written letter, and grammata the letters of the alphabet.
items.cn: 希腊语 gramma 意为字母，grammata 指整套字母。

items.en: Greek grammatike techne meant the art of letters, that is, the study of language.
items.cn: 希腊语 grammatike techne 意为文字之艺，即语言之学。

items.en: Latin grammatica carried the art-of-letters sense into scholarship.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grammatica 把文字之艺带入学问传统。

items.en: Old French gramaire passed the word on with both learning and magic tinges.
items.cn: 古法语 gramaire 传词时兼带学问与魔法色彩。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it as gramere; the rival spelling glamour kept the magic shade.
items.cn: 中古英语借作 gramere；竞争拼法 glamour 保留了魔法色彩。

items.en: Modern English fixed grammar for the rules, and grammar school named the old schools.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 grammar，grammar school 指旧式学校。

note.en: The words below resemble grammar in sound or share its learning field.
note.cn: 以下词与 grammar 音近，或同属语言学习义场。

entries.definition: Following the rules of grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合乎语法的」，由 grammar 派生。

entries.definition: Enchanting charm; historically the same word as grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「魅力」，与 grammar 历史上同源。

entries.definition: A unit of weight; one letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「克」，与 grammar 拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The arrangement of words in sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「句法」，语法的一部分。

entries.definition: The way words are actually used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「惯用法」，与规则互补。

entries.definition: The system of marks in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标点」，与语法并列的规则体系。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Greek gramma meant letter, the seed of grammar and diagram alike.
normal.cn: 希腊语 gramma 意为字母，是 grammar 与 diagram 的种子。

normal.cn: glamour 起初是 grammar 的苏格兰变体，意为魔法。

definition_zh: 污染；弄脏；玷污；亵渎；使（语言、数据等）变得不纯
definition_en: to put harmful or unwanted substances into air, water or land, or to make something impure, corrupted or ritually unclean
core_image: 一根排水管把暗色液体注进清澈的河湾，水面浮起一层油光，颜色从管口向外散开
scene: 排水管在夜里把暗色液体排进河湾，清晨水面上浮着一层油光。 The factory has polluted the bay for years without a permit.
sceneCN: 这里指向水体排放有害物质、使其变脏受损（第 1 个义项：向环境排入有害物质）；句意为这家工厂多年无证污染了海湾；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「污染；污染物」
由该动词加表示「进行者、物质」的名词尾构成，义为「污染物；污染物质」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「污染者；排污者」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受污染的」
由该动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「造成污染的」
由表示否定的前缀加已然形式构成，义为「未受污染的」
由表示否定的前缀加现在分词构成，义为「不造成污染的」

senses.title: To put harmful substances into the environment
senses.definition: to introduce substances or energy into air, water or soil in amounts that harm living things
senses.definitionCN: 把物质或能量引入空气、水体或土壤，其数量足以伤害生物
senses.example: Runoff from the fields has polluted the stream below the village.
senses.exampleCN: 田地的径流污染了村下游的小溪。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to soil or defile, and industry gave that soiling a physical target: air, water, ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是弄脏、玷污，工业给了这种弄脏一个物理对象：空气、水与土地。

senses.title: To make an object dirty or impure
senses.definition: to dirty or contaminate a concrete object so that it is no longer clean or usable
senses.definitionCN: 使一件具体物品变脏或混入杂质，以致不再洁净或可用
senses.example: Dust from the road polluted the open water tank.
senses.exampleCN: 路上的尘土弄脏了敞口的水箱。
senses.why: Before it named an environmental problem, the verb simply meant making a thing unclean.
senses.whyCN: 在它命名环境问题之前，这个动词只表示把东西弄得不再洁净。

senses.title: To desecrate something sacred
senses.definition: to treat a sacred place or rite as common or unclean, in religious and older legal usage
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教与旧式法律用法中，把圣地或圣礼当作凡俗或不洁之物对待
senses.example: The old law forbade anyone to pollute the spring used for the rite.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法禁止任何人玷污仪式所用的泉水。
senses.why: Defilement was a religious category long before it was a chemical one, and the verb kept that weight.
senses.whyCN: 「玷污」在成为化学范畴之前很久就是宗教范畴，这个动词保留了那份重量。

senses.title: To corrupt morals or a community
senses.definition: to degrade the moral character of a person, group or institution
senses.definitionCN: 败坏一个人、群体或制度的道德品质
senses.example: Critics claimed the broadcasts polluted the minds of the young.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者声称这些广播败坏了年轻人的心灵。
senses.why: If impurity can enter a body, it can enter a mind, and the metaphor moved from water to morals.
senses.whyCN: 既然杂质能进入身体，也能进入心灵，这个比喻就从水体移到了道德。

senses.title: To contaminate language or public debate
senses.definition: to fill speech, writing or public argument with falsehood, jargon or abuse until it loses clarity
senses.definitionCN: 让言语、文字或公共论辩充满虚假、行话或谩骂，以致失去清晰
senses.example: Readers said the comment threads had polluted the debate beyond repair.
senses.exampleCN: 读者说这些评论区已经把讨论污染到无法修复。
senses.why: Language is treated as a shared medium like water, and bad content spreads through it the same way.
senses.whyCN: 语言被当作像水一样的共享介质，坏内容以同样的方式在其中扩散。

senses.title: To disturb surroundings with noise or light
senses.titleCN: 以噪声或光干扰周围环境
senses.definition: to degrade an environment with excessive noise, artificial light or heat rather than a substance
senses.definitionCN: 用过量噪声、人工光或废热而不是物质，使环境质量下降
senses.example: The all-night floodlights polluted the darkness the moths depended on.
senses.exampleCN: 彻夜不熄的泛光灯破坏了蛾类赖以生存的黑暗环境。
senses.why: Once pollution meant any harmful addition, energy could pollute as well as matter.
senses.whyCN: 一旦污染被理解为任何有害添加，能量也能像物质一样造成污染。

senses.title: To insert errors into data or records
senses.titleCN: 在数据与记录中掺入错误
senses.definition: to add faulty, duplicated or misleading entries to a dataset or record
senses.definitionCN: 向数据集或记录中加入有误、重复或误导性的条目
senses.example: A bad script polluted the archive with thousands of duplicate rows.
senses.exampleCN: 一段有问题的脚本用成千上万条重复记录污染了档案库。
senses.why: Data is a reservoir that users share, and one bad input spreads through it.
senses.whyCN: 数据是用户共享的水库，一处坏输入就会在其中扩散。

senses.title: To contaminate water or food with pathogens
senses.titleCN: 以病原体污染水体或食物
senses.definition: to introduce bacteria, viruses or parasites into water or food so that it becomes unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 把细菌、病毒或寄生虫引入水或食物，使其不再安全
senses.example: The broken pipe polluted the well water with bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 破裂的管道用细菌污染了井水。
senses.why: Sanitation workers used the word for germs before environmental agencies used it for chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 卫生工作者比环境机构更早用这个词来说病菌。

senses.title: To be the source of pollution
senses.titleCN: 作为污染的来源与责任方
senses.definition: to cause pollution through discharge, leakage or careless practice, said of an operator
senses.definitionCN: 因排放、泄漏或操作不慎而造成污染，用于指作业者
senses.example: The plant polluted the river while its permit was under appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这家厂在许可证被申诉期间一直在污染这条河。
senses.why: Attribution matters legally, so the verb came to name the responsible actor as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 归责在法律上很重要，于是这个动词也用来指负有责任的行为者，而不只是行为。

intro.en: The word came into English through French from a Latin verb meaning to defile. Its parts are a prefix meaning forth and a stem usually connected with washing, a connection that scholars state as the usual view rather than a certainty.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语从拉丁语进入英语，原义为玷污。其构成是一个表示「向前」的前缀与一个通常与「洗」相联系的词干，学界对此只说「一般认为」，并非确证。

items.en: Luere meant to wash or cleanse, and it is usually taken as the second element of the Latin verb, though the link is stated as the usual view.
items.cn: 这个词意为洗、洗净，通常被认为是该拉丁动词的第二成分，不过这一联系只按通行的看法陈述。

items.en: The prefix, an assimilated form of the prefix for forth, added the idea of movement over a surface.
items.cn: 这个前缀是表示「向前」的前缀的同化形式，加上了在表面上移动的意思。

items.en: The verb meant to defile, contaminate or dishonour, and it was used of water, places and sacred things.
items.cn: 这个动词意为玷污、污染、使蒙羞，用于水体、场所与神圣之物。

items.en: The noun named the state of defilement, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 这个名词指被玷污的状态，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the verb onward, and English took it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词继续传下，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: The industrial age turned a word about defilement into a word about smoke, sewage and chemicals.
items.cn: 工业时代把关于玷污的词变成了关于烟尘、污水与化学品的词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stem; the second group names the acts and results of contaminating.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁词干；第二组是表示「污染行为与结果」的相邻说法。

entries.definition: The presence of harmful substances, and the act of introducing them.
entries.definitionCN: 指有害物质的存在，也指引入这些物质的行为。

entries.definition: A substance that pollutes when it enters the environment.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入环境后造成污染的物质。

entries.definition: The person or firm responsible for the pollution.
entries.definitionCN: 指对污染负有责任的人或企业。

entries.definition: Already contaminated, used of water, soil or air.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被污染的，用于水、土壤或空气。

entries.definition: To introduce something harmful, especially germs or a chemical, into a substance or place.
entries.definitionCN: 指向某物或某地引入有害的东西，尤指病菌或化学品。

entries.definition: To make unclean or to treat something sacred with disrespect.
entries.definitionCN: 指弄脏，或以不敬的方式对待神圣之物。

entries.definition: To spoil something by adding a trace of something bad, often used of food and reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 指因混入坏东西而使事物变坏，常用于食物与名誉。

entries.definition: To make something physically unclean, the plain everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指把东西弄脏的日常普通动词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the defilement sense, its recorded family and the modern environmental target.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「玷污」这一旧义、其有记录的词族与近代的环境对象。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to defile before it meant to pollute a river, and the older weight still shows in polluted reputation.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词先指玷污，后指污染河流，旧有的重量仍见于「名誉被玷污」。

normal.en: Pollution, pollutant, polluter and unpolluted all grow from one stem.
normal.cn: 污染、污染物、污染者与未受污染的，都从同一词干长出。

normal.en: Pollutant ends in a different suffix from pollute, which is why the two are often misspelled.
normal.cn: 污染物一词的词尾与动词不同，这正是两者常被拼错的原因。

normal.en: Heavily polluted is the fixed phrase used in reports about rivers and air.
normal.cn: 「受到严重污染的」是关于河流与空气的报告里的固定说法。

normal.en: The prefix means forth, so the verb pictures something carried out over a surface.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向前」，所以这个动词的画面是把东西铺到表面上。

abstract.en: Pollution is a cost pushed sideways: the maker keeps the product and gives the residue to everyone.
abstract.cn: 污染是被推向旁边的成本：制造者留下产品，把残渣交给所有人。

abstract.en: The same verb moves from water to minds to data because all three are shared media that one input can spoil.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词从水体移到心灵再移到数据，因为三者都是共享介质，一处输入就能弄坏。

abstract.en: Defilement is a boundary crossed: something clean and set apart has been made common.
abstract.cn: 玷污是一条边界被越过：本来洁净、被分隔开的东西被弄得凡俗了。

examples.en: The old smelter polluted the soil across three villages.
examples.cn: 那座旧冶炼厂污染了三个村庄的土壤。

examples.en: Discharge from the ships polluted the harbour with oil.
examples.cn: 船只的排放用油污染了港口。

examples.en: Editors warned that rumours had polluted the public record.
examples.cn: 编辑们警告说谣言已经污染了公共记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泼路特」——泼在路上，脏水泼进河里，就把水污染了；泼脏话，就把风气玷污了

root: 拉丁语 polluere「玷污、污染」← por-（向前，pro- 的同化形式）+ 词干 luere「洗」，后半与「洗」的联系一般认为是通行看法而非确证；名词 pollutio 为直接来源。英语十四世纪经古法语借入，先指玷污与亵渎，工业时代起指对空气、水体与土壤的污染。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep the old weight of defilement while moving outward: water and air, objects, sacred places, morals, language, noise and light, data, germs and the responsible actor.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保留「玷污」的旧重量并向外移动：水体与空气、器物、圣地、道德、语言、噪声与光、数据、病菌，以及负有责任的行为者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe pours dark liquid into a clear bay, and the colour spreads outward from the mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根管子把暗色液体倒进清澈的海湾，颜色从管口向外散开。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SPOILING: harmful inputs into air, water and soil, and dirt added to a plain object.
branches.cn: 物理弄脏：有害输入进入空气、水与土壤，以及加到普通器物上的污物。

branches.en: THE INWARD DEFILEMENT: sacred places treated as common, and morals treated as a body that impurity can enter.
branches.cn: 向内的玷污：被当作凡俗的圣地，以及被当作可让杂质进入的道德。

branches.en: THE SHARED MEDIUM: language and public debate, and datasets filled with bad entries.
branches.cn: 共享介质：语言与公共讨论，以及被坏条目填满的数据集。

branches.en: THE OTHER CARRIERS: noise and light, and germs in water or food.
branches.cn: 其他载体：噪声与光，以及水体或食物中的病菌。

branches.en: THE LEDGER OF BLAME: the operator who discharges and is named as the source.
branches.cn: 责任账目：实施排放并被指名为来源的作业者。

intro.en: A prefix for forth and a stem usually read as washing make the Latin verb; English derived a whole family from it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「向前」的前缀与一个通常读作「洗」的词干构成拉丁动词，英语由此派生了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb, its noun and its participle; the reading of the second element as washing is the usual view, not a certainty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了动词、名词与分词；把第二成分读作「洗」是通行看法，并非确证。

items.example: The verb carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都由这个动词承载。

items.example: It pictures something carried out over a surface.
items.exampleCN: 它画出把东西铺到表面上的画面。

items.example: It is the usual reading of the second element.
items.exampleCN: 这是对第二成分的通行解读。

items.example: It is the recorded direct source.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的直接来源。

items.example: It makes the word for a polluting substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示污染物质的词。

items.example: It makes the word for the responsible party.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示责任方的词。

items.example: It marks water or air that is still clean.
items.exampleCN: 它标记仍然洁净的水或空气。
